children.text: Chapter 1
dikkālādyanavacchinnānantacinmātramūrtaye
children.translated_text: Homage to that peaceful radiance, whose form is pure endless consciousness, unlimited by direction, time, and the like,

children.text: svānubhūtyekamānāya namaḥ śāntāya tejase ||
children.translated_text: and which is measured only by one's own experience.

children.text: boddhāro matsaragrastāḥ prabhavaḥ smayadūṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who understand are seized by envy; the powerful are spoiled by pride;

children.text: abodhopahatāḥ cānye jīrṇam aṅge subhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: and others are struck down by ignorance. Thus the well-spoken saying has grown old in my body.

children.text: ajñaḥ sukham ārādhyaḥ sukhataram ārādhyate viśeṣajñaḥ
children.translated_text: An ignorant man is easily pleased; one who has special knowledge is pleased still more easily;

children.text: jñānalavadurvidagdhaṃ brahmāpi taṃ naraṃ na rañjayati ||
children.translated_text: but even <s>Brahmā</s> cannot delight the man made arrogant by a little scrap of knowledge.

children.text: prasahya maṇim uddharen makaravaktradaṃṣṭrāntarāt samudram api saṃtaret pracaladūrmimālākulam
children.translated_text: One may forcibly draw a jewel out from between the teeth in a crocodile's mouth, and may even cross the ocean, crowded with a garland of tossing waves;

children.text: bhujaṅgam api kopitaṃ śirasi puṣpavad dhārayet na tu pratiniviṣṭamūrkhajanacittam ārādhayet ||
children.translated_text: one may bear even an enraged serpent on one's head like a flower, but one should not try to please the mind of an obstinate fool.

children.text: labheta sikatāsu tailam api yatnataḥ pīḍayan pibecca mṛgatṛṣṇikāsu salilaṃ pipāsārditaḥ
children.translated_text: By effort one might press oil even from sand; afflicted by thirst, one might drink water in a mirage;

children.text: kvacid api paryaṭan śaśaviṣāṇam āsādayet na tu pratiniviṣṭamūrkhacittam ārādhayet ||
children.translated_text: wandering somewhere, one might even obtain a hare's horn, but one should not try to please the mind of an obstinate fool.

children.text: vyālaṃ bālamṛṇālatantubhir asau roddhuṃ samujjṛmbhate chettuṃ vajramaṇiṃ śirīṣakusumaprāntena saṃnahyati
children.translated_text: That man makes ready to restrain a snake with threads from a tender lotus-stalk; he arms himself to cut a diamond with the tip of a śirīṣa flower;

children.text: mādhuryaṃ madhubindunā racayituṃ kṣārāmudher īhate netuṃ vāñchati yaḥ khalān pathi satāṃ sūktaiḥ sudhāsyandibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: he strives to make the salty ocean sweet with a drop of honey, who wishes to lead the wicked onto the path of the good with sayings that stream with nectar.

children.text: svāyattam ekāntaguṇaṃ vidhātrā vinirmitaṃ chādanam ajñatāyāḥ
children.translated_text: Silence, created by the Creator as a covering for ignorance, is under one's own control and has a single excellent quality;

children.text: viśeṣataḥ sarvavidāṃ samāje vibhūṣaṇaṃ maunam apaṇḍitānām ||
children.translated_text: especially in an assembly of the learned, it is the ornament of the unlearned.

children.text: yadā kiṃcijjño 'haṃ dvipa iva madāndhaḥ samabhavaṃ tadā sarvajño 'smīty abhavad avaliptaṃ mama manaḥ
children.translated_text: When I knew a little, I became blind with arrogance like an elephant in rut; then my mind, puffed up, thought, 'I know everything.'

children.text: yadā kiṃcitkiṃcidbudhajanasakāśād avagataṃ tadā mūrkho 'smīti jvara iva mado me vyapagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: When I learned a little bit from the presence of wise people, then, like a fever, my intoxication departed: 'I am a fool.'

children.text: kṛmikulacitaṃ lālāklinnaṃ vigandhi jugupsitaṃ nirupamarasaṃ prītyā khādan narāsthi nirāmiṣam
children.translated_text: A dog, fondly eating a meatless human bone, full of worms, wet with saliva, foul-smelling, disgusting, and without any incomparable taste,

children.text: surapatim api śvā pārśvasthaṃ vilokya na śaṅkate na hi gaṇayati kṣudro jantuḥ parigrahaphalgutām ||
children.translated_text: does not feel alarm even when he sees the lord of the gods standing nearby; for a low creature does not reckon the worthlessness of its possession.

children.text: śiraḥ śārvaṃ svargāt paśupatiśirastaḥ kṣitidharaṃ mahīdhrād uttuṅgād avanim avaneś cāpi jaladhim
children.translated_text: The head of <s>Śarva</s>; from heaven to the head of <s>Paśupati</s>, from there to the mountain, from the lofty mountain to the earth, and from the earth too to the ocean:

children.text: adho 'dho gaṅgeyaṃ padam upagatā stokam athavā vivekabhraṣṭānāṃ bhavati vinipātaḥ śatamukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Gaṅgā</s> went step by step downward. Indeed, for those whose discernment has failed, the fall has a hundred openings.

children.text: śakyo vārayituṃ jalena hutabhuk chatreṇa sūryātapo nāgendro niśitāṅkuśena samado daṇḍena gogardabhau
children.translated_text: Fire can be restrained with water, the sun's heat with a parasol, a rutting lordly elephant with a sharp goad, and cows and donkeys with a stick;

children.text: vyādhir bheṣajasaṅgrahaiś ca vividhair mantraprayogair viṣaṃ sarvasyauṣadham asti śāstravihitaṃ mūrkhasya nāstyauṣadham ||
children.translated_text: disease can be checked with collections of medicines, and poison with various applications of mantras. For everything there is a remedy prescribed by śāstra (authoritative teaching); for a fool there is no remedy.

children.text: sāhityasaṃgītakalāvihīnaḥ sākṣāt paśuḥ pucchaviṣāṇahīnaḥ
children.translated_text: A man devoid of literature, music, and the arts is plainly a beast without tail and horns;

children.text: tṛṇaṃ na khādann api jīvamānastad bhāgadheyaṃ paramaṃ paśūnām ||
children.translated_text: though he lives without eating grass, that is the supreme good fortune of beasts.

children.text: yeṣāṃ na vidyā na tapo na dānaṃ jñānaṃ na śīlaṃ na guṇo na dharmaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who have no learning, no ascetic discipline, no giving, no knowledge, no character, no virtue, and no dharma (right conduct),

children.text: te martyaloke bhuvi bhārabhūtā manuṣyarūpeṇa mṛgāś caranti ||
children.translated_text: are burdens upon the earth in the mortal world; they wander about as animals in human form.

children.text: varaṃ parvatadurgeṣu bhrāntaṃ vanacaraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Better to wander in mountain fastnesses together with forest-dwellers

children.text: na mūrkhajanasamparkaḥ surendrabhavaneṣv api ||
children.translated_text: than to have contact with foolish people, even in the palaces of the lord of the gods.

children.text: śāstropaskṛtaśabdasundaragiraḥ śiṣyapradeyāgamā vikhyātāḥ kavayo vasanti viṣaye yasya prabhor nirdhanāḥ
children.translated_text: If famous poets, whose beautiful speech is adorned by śāstra and whose tradition is to be handed to pupils, live poor in a ruler's territory,

children.text: tajjāḍyaṃ vasudhādhipasya kavayas tvarthaṃ vināpīśvarāḥ kutsyāḥ syuḥ kuparīkṣakā hi maṇayo yair arghataḥ pātitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is the dullness of the king of the earth; poets are lords even without wealth. For jewels become blameworthy through bad appraisers, by whom they are lowered in price.

children.text: hartur yāti na gocaraṃ kim api śaṃ puṣṇāti yat sarvadā 'pyarthibhyaḥ pratipādyamānam aniśaṃ prāpnoti vṛddhiṃ parām
children.translated_text: It does not come within a thief's range; it always nourishes some good; when constantly bestowed upon petitioners, it attains the highest increase;

children.text: kalpānteṣvapi na prayāti nidhanaṃ vidyākhyam antardhanaṃ yeṣāṃ tān prati mānam ujhata nṛpāḥ kas taiḥ saha spardhate ||
children.translated_text: even at the ends of aeons it does not perish: this inner wealth called learning. Kings, abandon pride toward those who possess it. Who can compete with them?

children.text: adhigataparamārthān paṇḍitān māvamaṃsthāstṛṇam iva laghu lakṣmīr naiva tān saṃruṇaddhi
children.translated_text: Do not despise learned men who have grasped the highest truth; wealth, light as straw, never restrains them.

children.text: abhinavamadalekhāśyāmagaṇḍasthalānāṃ na bhavati bisatantur vāraṇaṃ vāraṇānām ||
children.translated_text: A lotus-fiber does not become a restraint for elephants whose cheek-regions are darkened by fresh streaks of rut.

children.text: ambhojinīvanavihāravilāsam eva haṃsasya hanti nitarāṃ kupito vidhātā
children.translated_text: An angry Creator may utterly destroy only the swan's graceful sport of wandering in a lotus-pond;

children.text: na tvasya dugdhajalabhedavidhau prasiddhāṃ vaidagdhīkīrtim apahartum asau samarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but he is not able to take away its famed skillful reputation in the matter of separating milk from water.

children.text: keyūrāṇi na bhūṣayanti puruṣaṃ hārā na candrojjvalā na snānaṃ na vilepanaṃ na kusumaṃ nālaṃkṛtā mūrdhajāḥ
children.translated_text: Armlets do not adorn a man, nor necklaces bright as the moon, nor bathing, nor ointment, nor flowers, nor hair elaborately dressed.

children.text: vāṇyekā samalaṃkaroti puruṣaṃ yā saṃskṛtā dhāryate kṣīyante khalu bhūṣaṇāni satataṃ vāgbhūṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Cultivated speech alone adorns a man when it is borne; ornaments certainly decay forever, but the ornament of speech is the ornament.

children.text: vidyā nāma narasya rūpam adhikaṃ pracchannaguptaṃ dhanaṃ vidyā bhogakarī yaśaḥsukhakarī vidyā gurūṇāṃ guruḥ
children.translated_text: Learning is the higher beauty of a man, a hidden and guarded treasure; learning brings enjoyment, fame, and happiness; learning is the teacher of teachers.

children.text: vidyā bandhujano videśagamane vidyā parā devatā vidyā rājasu pūjyate na tu dhanaṃ vidyāvihīnaḥ paśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Learning is kin when one goes abroad; learning is the supreme divinity; learning is honored among kings, not wealth; one without learning is a beast.

children.text: kṣāntiś cet kavacena kiṃ kim aribhiḥ krodho 'sti ced dehināṃ jñātiśced analena kiṃ yadi suhṛd divyauṣadhaṃ kimphalam
children.translated_text: If there is forbearance, what need of armor? What use are enemies if embodied beings have anger? If there is a kinsman, what need of fire? If there is a friend, what is the use of a divine medicine?

children.text: kiṃ sarpair yadi durjanāḥ kimu dhanair vidyā 'navadyā yadi vrīḍā cet kimu bhūṣaṇaiḥ sukavitā yady asti rājyena kim ||
children.translated_text: What use are snakes, if there are wicked men? What use is wealth, if there is faultless learning? If there is modesty, what use are ornaments? If there is good poetry, what use is kingship?

children.text: dākṣiṇyaṃ svajane dayā parijane śāṭhyaṃ sadā durjane prītiḥ sādhujane nayo nṛpajane vidvajjane cārjavam
children.translated_text: Kindness toward one's own people, compassion toward attendants, constant cunning toward the wicked, affection toward good people, policy toward kings, and straightforwardness toward the learned;

children.text: śauryaṃ śatrujane kṣamā gurujane kāntājane dhṛṣṭatā ye caivaṃ puruṣāḥ kalāsu kuśalās teṣv eva lokasthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: courage toward enemies, patience toward elders, boldness toward the beloved: only among men who are skilled in such arts does the stability of the world exist.

children.text: jāḍyaṃ dhiyo harati siñcati vāci satyaṃ mānonnatiṃ diśati pāpam apākaroti
children.translated_text: It removes dullness from the intellect, pours truth into speech, grants elevation of honor, and drives away sin.

children.text: cetaḥ prasādayati dikṣu tanoti kīrtiṃ satsaṅgatiḥ kathaya kiṃ na karoti puṃsām ||
children.translated_text: It gladdens the mind and spreads fame in all directions: tell me, what does association with the good not do for men?

children.text: jayanti te sukṛtino rasasiddhāḥ kavīśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: Victorious are those meritorious lords of poets, perfected in rasa;

children.text: nāsti yeṣāṃ yaśaḥkāye jarāmaraṇajaṃ bhayam ||
children.translated_text: for in the body of their fame there is no fear born of old age and death.

children.text: sūnuḥ saccaritaḥ satī priyatamā svāmī prasādonmukhaḥ snigdhaṃ mitram avañcakaḥ parijano niḥkleśaleśaṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: A son of good conduct, a faithful beloved wife, a master inclined to favor, an affectionate friend, attendants who do not deceive, a mind without the least trace of distress,

children.text: ākāro ruciraḥ sthiraś ca vibhavo vidyāvadātaṃ mukhaṃ tuṣṭe viṣṭapakaṣṭahāriṇi harau samprāpyate dehinā ||
children.translated_text: a handsome form, stable prosperity, and a face bright with learning: these are obtained by an embodied being when <s>Hari</s>, remover of the world's distress, is pleased.

children.text: prāṇāghātān nivṛttiḥ paradhanaharaṇe saṃyamaḥ satyavākyaṃ kāle śaktyā pradānaṃ yuvatijanakathāmūkabhāvaḥ pareṣām
children.translated_text: Abstention from taking life, restraint in stealing another's wealth, truthful speech, giving at the right time according to one's power, silence about others' women,

children.text: tṛṣṇāsroto vibhaṅgo guruṣu ca vinayaḥ sarvabhūtānukampā sāmānyaḥ sarvaśāstreṣv anupahatavidhiḥ śreyasām eṣa panthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: breaking the stream of craving, humility toward teachers, and compassion for all beings: this is the common, unimpaired rule in all śāstras, the path of the highest goods.

children.text: prārabhyate na khalu vighnabhayena nīcaiḥ prārabhya vighnavihatā viramanti madhyāḥ
children.translated_text: Inferior people do not begin because of fear of obstacles; middling people begin, but stop when struck down by obstacles.

children.text: vighnaiḥ punaḥ punar api pratihanyamānāḥ prārabdham uttamajanā na parityajanti ||
children.translated_text: Even when checked again and again by obstacles, excellent people do not abandon what they have begun.

children.text: asanto nābhyarthyāḥ suhṛd api na yācyaḥ kṛśadhanaḥ priyā nyāyyā vṛttir malinam asubhaṅge 'pyasukaram
children.translated_text: The bad are not to be entreated; even a friend who has little wealth is not to be begged from; a lawful livelihood is dear, though difficult when one's body is worn and soiled.

children.text: vipady uccaiḥ stheyaṃ padam anuvidheyaṃ ca mahatāṃ satāṃ kenoddiṣṭaṃ viṣamam asidhārāvratam idam ||
children.translated_text: In misfortune one must stand high; one must follow the path of the great. By whom was this hard sword-edge vow of the good prescribed?

children.text: kṣutkṣāmo 'pi jarākṛśo 'pi śithilaprāṇo 'pi kaṣṭāṃ daśāmāpanno 'pi vipannadīdhitir iti prāṇeṣu naśyatsv api
children.translated_text: Though emaciated by hunger, though wasted by age, though his life-breath is weak, though he has fallen into a harsh condition, though his brilliance is gone, even while his life-breaths are perishing,

children.text: mattebhendravibhinnakumbhapiśitagrāsaikabaddhaspṛhaḥ kiṃ jīrṇaṃ tṛṇam atti mānamahatām agresaraḥ kesarī ||
children.translated_text: will a lion, foremost among the honorable, whose desire is fixed only on mouthfuls of flesh from the temples split open on rutting lordly elephants, eat dry grass?

children.text: svalpasnāyuvasāvaśeṣamalinaṃ nirmāṃsam apyasthi goḥ śvā labdhvā paritoṣam eti na tu tat tasya kṣudhāśāntaye
children.translated_text: A dog, having found the filthy bone of an ox, with only a little sinew and fat remaining and no flesh, is satisfied, though it cannot quiet his hunger.

children.text: siṃho jambukam aṅkam āgatam api tyaktvā nihanti dvipaṃ sarvaḥ kṛcchragato 'pi vāñchati janaḥ sattvānurūpaṃ phalam ||
children.translated_text: But a lion, leaving aside even a jackal that has come into his lap, kills an elephant: every person, even when reduced to hardship, desires a reward suited to his own nature.

children.text: lāṅgūlacālanam adhaścaraṇāvapātaṃ bhūmau nipatya vadanodaradarśanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Wagging the tail, dropping down beneath the feet, falling on the ground, and showing the mouth and belly:

children.text: śvā piṇḍadasya kurute gajapuṅgavas tu dhīraṃ vilokayati cāṭuśataiś ca bhuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: a dog does this for the giver of a morsel, but the best of elephants looks on steadily and eats only after hundreds of flatteries.

children.text: parivartini saṃsāre mṛtaḥ ko vā na jāyate
children.translated_text: In this changing world, who that has died is not born again?

children.text: sa jāto yena jātena yāti vaṃśaḥ samunnatim ||
children.translated_text: He alone is truly born by whose birth the family rises to eminence.

children.text: kusumastabakasyeva dvayī vṛttir manasvinaḥ
children.translated_text: Like a cluster of flowers, the high-minded person has two possible courses:

children.text: mūrdhni vā sarvalokasya śīryate vana eva vā ||
children.translated_text: either he is placed on the head of all the world, or he withers away in the forest alone.

children.text: santy anye 'pi bṛhaspatiprabhṛtayaḥ saṃbhāvitāḥ pañcaṣāstān pratyeṣa viśeṣavikramarucī rāhur na vairāyate
children.translated_text: There are other respected ones also, beginning with <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, five or six; toward them <s>Rāhu</s>, who delights in special prowess, feels no hostility.

children.text: dvāveva grasate divākaraniśāprāṇeśvarau bhāskarau bhrātaḥ parvaṇi paśya dānavapatiḥ śīrṣāvaśeṣākṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He seizes only the two luminous lords, the sun and the moon, life-masters of day and night. Brother, look at the lord of demons at eclipse-time, his form reduced to a head.

children.text: vahati bhuvanaśreṇiṃ śeṣaḥ phaṇāphalakasthitāṃ kamaṭhapatinā madhyepṛṣṭhaṃ sadā sa ca dhāryate
children.translated_text: <s>Śeṣa</s> bears the row of worlds placed upon the plates of his hoods, and he in turn is always supported on the middle of the back by the lord of tortoises.

children.text: tam api kurute kroḍādhīnaṃ payodhir anādarād ahaha mahatāṃ niḥsīmānaścaritravibhūtayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ocean, with disregard, makes even him subject to its hollow. Ah, the majestic powers of the great are without limit.

children.text: varaṃ pakṣacchedaḥ samadamaghavanmuktakuliśaprahārair udgacchadbahuladahanodgāragurubhiḥ
children.translated_text: Better the cutting off of the wings by the heavy blows of the thunderbolt released by exultant <s>Maghavan</s>, with abundant flames leaping forth,

children.text: tuṣārādreḥ sūnor ahaha pitari kleśavivaśe na cāsau sampātaḥ payasi payasāṃ patyur ucitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: than for the son of the snowy mountain, while his father is helpless in distress, to fall into the waters of the lord of waters. That would not be fitting.

children.text: siṃhaḥ śiśur api nipatati madamalinakapolabhittiṣu gajeṣu
children.translated_text: A lion, even as a cub, leaps upon elephants whose temple-walls are stained with rut.

children.text: prakṛtir iyaṃ sattvavatāṃ na khalu vayas tejaso hetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the nature of the spirited: age is certainly not the cause of splendor.

children.text: jātir yātu rasātalaṃ guṇagaṇais tatrāpy adho gamyatāṃ śīlaṃ śailataṭāt patatvabhijanaḥ saṃdahyatāṃ vahninā
children.translated_text: Let birth go to the netherworld; let the multitude of virtues go even lower there; let character fall from a mountain slope; let noble lineage be burned by fire.

children.text: śaurye vairiṇi vajram āśu nipatatv artho 'stu naḥ kevalaṃ yenaikena vinā guṇas tṛṇalavaprāyāḥ samastā ime ||
children.translated_text: Let a thunderbolt quickly fall on courage as its enemy; let wealth alone be ours, for without that one thing all these qualities are like mere bits of grass.

children.text: dhanam arjaya kākutstha dhanamūlam idaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: Acquire wealth, O <s>Kākutstha</s>; this world has wealth as its root.

children.text: antaraṃ nābhijānāmi nirdhanasya mṛtasya ca ||
children.translated_text: I perceive no difference between a poor man and a dead man.

children.text: tānīndriyāṇyavikalāni tad eva nāma sā buddhir apratihatā vacanaṃ tad eva
children.translated_text: Those very senses remain unimpaired, that same name remains, that intellect is unobstructed, and that speech is the same;

children.text: arthoṣmaṇā virahitaḥ puruṣaḥ kṣaṇena so 'pyanya eva bhavatīti vicitram etat ||
children.translated_text: yet a man deprived of the warmth of wealth becomes, in a moment, someone altogether different. This is strange indeed.

children.text: yasyāsti vittaṃ sa naraḥ kulīnaḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ sa śrutavān guṇajñaḥ
children.translated_text: The man who has money is well-born; he is learned; he is versed in scripture; he knows virtues.

children.text: sa eva vaktā sa ca darśanīyaḥ sarve guṇāḥ kāñcanam āśrayanti ||
children.translated_text: He alone is eloquent, and he is worth seeing: all qualities take refuge in gold.

children.text: daurmantryān nṛpatir vinaśyati yatiḥ saṅgāt suto lālanāt vipro 'nadhyayanāt kulaṃ kutanayācchīlaṃ khalopāsanāt
children.translated_text: Through bad counsel a king is ruined; an ascetic through attachment; a son through indulgence; a learned Brahmin through neglect of study; a family through a bad woman; character through service to the wicked.

children.text: hrīr madyād anavekṣaṇād api kṛṣiḥ snehaḥ pravāsāśrayān maitrī cāpraṇayāt samṛddhir anayāt tyāgapramādād dhanam ||
children.translated_text: Modesty is ruined by liquor; even agriculture by lack of oversight; affection by dependence on travel abroad; friendship by lack of love; prosperity by bad policy; wealth by careless failure to give.

children.text: dānaṃ bhogo nāśas tisro gatayo bhavanti vittasya
children.translated_text: Giving, enjoyment, and destruction: these are the three courses of wealth.

children.text: yo na dadāti na bhuṅkte tasya tṛtīyā gatir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For one who neither gives nor enjoys, the third course is what comes to his wealth.

children.text: maṇiḥ śāṇollīḍhaḥ samaravijayī hetidalito madakṣīṇo nāgaḥ śaradi saritaḥ śyānapulināḥ
children.translated_text: A jewel polished on the whetstone, a warrior victorious in battle though cut by weapons, an elephant whose rut has ebbed, rivers in autumn with their banks exposed,

children.text: kalāśeṣaś candraḥ suratamṛditā bālavanitā tannimnā śobhante galitavibhavāś cārthiṣu narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the moon with only a digit remaining, a young woman wearied by love-play, and men whose wealth has slipped away through petitioners: these shine precisely in that lowered state.

children.text: parikṣīṇaḥ kaścit spṛhayati yavānāṃ prasṛtaye sa paścāt sampūrṇaḥ kalayati dharitrīṃ tṛṇasamām
children.translated_text: Someone impoverished longs for a mere handful of barley; afterwards, when full, he reckons the earth as equal to grass.

children.text: ataś cānaikāntyād gurulaghutayā 'rtheṣu dhaninām avasthā vastūni prathayati ca saṃkocayati ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus, because there is no fixed rule about greatness and smallness in matters of wealth, the condition of rich men both expands and contracts things.

children.text: rājan dudhukṣasi yadi kṣitidhenum etāṃ tenādya vatsam iva lokam amuṃ puṣāṇa
children.translated_text: O king, if you wish to milk this earth-cow, then today nourish this people as one would a calf.

children.text: tasmiṃśca samyag aniśaṃ paripoṣyamāṇe nānāphalaiḥ phalati kalpalateva bhūmiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When that calf is properly nourished without cease, the earth bears fruit with many fruits, like a wish-fulfilling creeper.

children.text: satyānṛtā ca paruṣā priyavādinī ca hiṃsrā dayālur api cārthaparā vadānyā
children.translated_text: Truthful and false, harsh and sweet-speaking, violent and compassionate, intent on wealth and generous,

children.text: nityavyayā pracuranityadhanāgamā ca vārāṅganeva nṛpanītir anekarūpā ||
children.translated_text: always spending, yet also bringing in abundant constant wealth: royal policy is many-formed, like a courtesan.

children.text: ājñā kīrtiḥ pālanaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ dānaṃ bhogo mitrasaṃrakṣaṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Command, fame, protection of Brahmins, giving, enjoyment, and preservation of friends:

children.text: yeṣām ete ṣaḍguṇā na pravṛttāḥ ko 'rthas teṣāṃ pārthivopāśrayeṇa ||
children.translated_text: for those in whom these six qualities have not appeared, what is the use of taking refuge in kingship?

children.text: yad dhātrā nijabhālapaṭṭalikhitaṃ stokaṃ mahad vā dhanaṃ tat prāpnoti marusthale 'pi nitarāṃ merau tato nādhikam
children.translated_text: Whatever wealth, small or great, the Creator has written on one's own forehead-plate, that one obtains even in a desert; on <s>Meru</s> one obtains no more than that.

children.text: tad dhīro bhava vittavatsu kṛpaṇāṃ vṛttiṃ vṛthā sā kṛthāḥ kūpe paśya payonidhāvapi ghaṭo gṛhṇāti tulyaṃ jalam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore be steadfast. Do not vainly adopt a pitiable manner toward the wealthy. Look: in a well and even in the ocean, a jar takes up the same amount of water.

children.text: tvam eva cātakādhāro 'sīti keṣāṃ na gocaraḥ
children.translated_text: 'You alone are the support of the <s>cātaka</s> bird' - to whom is this not evident?

children.text: kim ambhodavarāsmākaṃ kārpaṇyoktaṃ pratīkṣase ||
children.translated_text: O best of clouds, why do you wait for our miserable statement of poverty?

children.text: re re cātaka sāvadhānamanasā mitra kṣaṇaṃ śrūyatām ambhodā bahavo vasanti gagane sarve 'pi naitādṛśāḥ
children.translated_text: Hey, hey, <s>cātaka</s>, friend, listen for a moment with an attentive mind: many clouds dwell in the sky; not all are of this kind.

children.text: kecid vṛṣṭibhir ārdrayanti vasudhāṃ garjanti kecid vṛthā yaṃ yaṃ paśyasi tasya tasya purato mā brūhi dīnaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some moisten the earth with showers; some merely thunder in vain. Do not utter a wretched speech before each and every one you see.

children.text: akaruṇatvam akāraṇavigrahaḥ paradhane parayoṣiti ca spṛhā
children.translated_text: Pitilessness, causeless quarrel, desire for another's wealth and another's wife,

children.text: sujanabandhujaneṣv asahiṣṇutā prakṛtisiddham idaṃ hi durātmanām ||
children.translated_text: and intolerance toward good people and relatives: this indeed belongs by nature to the wicked.

children.text: durjanaḥ parihartavyo vidyayālaṃkṛto 'pi san
children.translated_text: A bad man should be avoided, even if he is adorned with learning.

children.text: maṇinā bhūṣitaḥ sarpaḥ kim asau na bhayaṅkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Is a snake adorned with a jewel not frightening?

children.text: jāḍyaṃ hrīmati gaṇyate vratarucau dambhaḥ śucau kaitavaṃ śūre nirghṛṇatā munau vimatitā dainyaṃ priyālāpini
children.translated_text: In a modest man they count dullness; in one devoted to vows, hypocrisy; in the pure, deceit; in the brave, cruelty; in a sage, wrong thinking; in one who speaks pleasantly, wretchedness;

children.text: tejasviny avaliptatā mukharatā vaktaryaśaktiḥ sthire tat ko nāma guṇo bhavet sa guṇināṃ yo durjanair nāṅkitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the spirited, arrogance; in an eloquent speaker, talkativeness; in the firm, incapacity. What quality, then, could there be among the virtuous that is not branded by wicked people?

children.text: lobhaś ced aguṇena kiṃ piśunatā yady asti kiṃ pātakaiḥ satyaṃ cet tapasā ca kiṃ śuci mano yadyasti tīrthena kim
children.translated_text: If there is greed, what need is there of another vice? If slander exists, what need is there of sins? If truth exists, what need is there of austerity? If the mind is pure, what need is there of a pilgrimage-place?

children.text: saujanyaṃ yadi kiṃ guṇaiḥ sumahimā yadyasti kiṃ maṇḍanaiḥ sadvidyā yadi kiṃ dhanair apayaśo yadyasti kiṃ mṛtyunā ||
children.translated_text: If there is goodness, what need is there of other virtues? If there is great glory, what need is there of ornaments? If there is true learning, what need is there of riches? If there is disgrace, what need is there of death?

children.text: śaśī divasadhūsaro galitayauvanā kāminī saro vigatavārijaṃ mukham anakṣaraṃ svākṛteḥ
children.translated_text: A moon made dim by day, a woman whose youth has passed, a lake without lotuses, a face without letters though handsome in form,

children.text: prabhur dhanaparāyaṇaḥ satatadurgataḥ sajjano nṛpāṅgaṇagataḥ khalo manasi sapta śalyāni me ||
children.translated_text: a lord devoted to wealth, a good man always in distress, and a wicked man gone into the king's courtyard: these seven are thorns in my mind.

children.text: na kaściccaṇḍakopānām ātmīyo nāma bhūbhujām
children.translated_text: For earth-ruling kings of fierce anger there is no one called their own.

children.text: hotāram api juhvānaṃ spṛṣṭo vahati pāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fire burns even the priest who is offering oblations when he is touched by it.

children.text: maunomūkaḥ pravacanapaṭur vātulo jalpako vā dhṛṣṭaḥ pārśve vasati ca sadā dūrataś cāpragalbhaḥ
children.translated_text: If silent, he is dumb; if skilled in speech, he is mad or a chatterer; if bold, he always lives too close at hand; if he stays at a distance, he is not confident;

children.text: kṣāntyā bhīruryadi na sahate prāyaśo nābhijātaḥ sevādharmaḥ paramagahano yoginām apyagamyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: if patient, he is timid; if he does not endure, he is generally not well-born. The duty of service is exceedingly deep, inaccessible even to yogins.

children.text: udbhāsitākhilakhalasya viśṛṅkhalasya prāgjātavistṛtanijādhamakarmavṛtteḥ
children.translated_text: For this base man, who hates virtues, whose whole wickedness is manifest, who is unrestrained, whose conduct in low deeds has long since spread abroad,

children.text: daivād avāptavibhavasya guṇadviṣo 'sya nīcasya gocaragataiḥ sukham āpyate ||
children.translated_text: and who has obtained prosperity by fate, happiness is gained by those who come within his range.

children.text: ārambhagurvī kṣayiṇī krameṇa laghvī purā vṛddhimatī ca paścāt
children.translated_text: The friendship of the wicked and the good is like shadow, divided between the first and latter halves of the day: heavy at the beginning and gradually diminishing; light before, and later increasing.

children.text: dinasya pūrvārdhaparārdhabhinnā chāyeva maitrī khalasajjanānām ||
children.translated_text: The friendship of the wicked and the good is like a shadow, different in the first and second halves of the day.

children.text: mṛgamīnasajjanānāṃ tṛṇajalasantoṣavihitavṛttīnām
children.translated_text: Deer, fish, and good people live lives made content with grass, water, and satisfaction.

children.text: lubdhakadhīvarapiśunā niṣkāraṇavairiṇo jagati ||
children.translated_text: Yet in this world hunters, fishermen, and slanderers are their causeless enemies.

children.text: vāñchā sajjanasaṅgame paraguṇe prītir gurau namratā vidyāyāṃ vyasanaṃ svayoṣiti ratir lokāpavādād bhayam
children.translated_text: Desire for the company of good people, delight in the virtues of others, humility toward the teacher, devotion to learning, love for one's own wife, fear of public reproach,

children.text: bhaktiḥ śūlini śaktir ātmadamane saṃsargamuktiḥ khale yeṣvete nivasanti nirmalaguṇās tebhyo narebhyo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: devotion to <s>Śūlin</s>, power in self-control, and freedom from association with the wicked: reverence to those people in whom these stainless virtues dwell.

children.text: vipadi dhairyam athābhyudaye kṣamā sadasi vākyapaṭutā yudhi vikramaḥ
children.translated_text: Courage in adversity, forbearance in prosperity, skill in speech in an assembly, valor in battle,

children.text: yaśasi cābhirucir vyasanaṃ śrutau prakṛtisiddham idaṃ hi mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: delight in fame, and devotion to scripture: this indeed is innate in great souls.

children.text: pradānaṃ pracchannaṃ gṛham upagate sambhramavidhiḥ priyaṃ kṛtvā maunaṃ sadasi kathanaṃ cāpyupakṛteḥ
children.translated_text: Giving in secret; when someone comes to one's house, the performance of hospitable attentions with eagerness; having done a kindness, keeping silence about it; yet in an assembly, speaking of another's kindness;

children.text: anutseko lakṣmyām anabhibhavagandhāḥ parakathāḥ satāṃ kenoddiṣṭaṃ viṣamam asidhārāvratam idam ||
children.translated_text: not becoming arrogant in prosperity; speaking about others without the slightest trace of contempt: who has prescribed this difficult vow of good people, like walking on the edge of a sword?

children.text: kare ślāghyas tyāgaḥ śirasi gurupādapraṇayitā mukhe satyā vāṇī vijayi bhujayor vīryam atulam
children.translated_text: In the hand, praiseworthy renunciation; on the head, loving devotion to the feet of the guru; in the mouth, truthful speech; in the victorious arms, unequalled heroism;

children.text: hṛdi svacchā vṛttiḥ śrutim adhigataṃ ca śravaṇayorvināpyaiśvaryeṇa prakṛtimahatāṃ maṇḍanam idam ||
children.translated_text: in the heart, a pure disposition; and in the ears, learning that has been acquired from scripture: even without wealth, this is the adornment of those who are great by nature.

children.text: saṃpatsu mahatāṃ cittaṃ bhavaty utpalakomalam
children.translated_text: In good fortune the mind of the great becomes soft as a lotus;

children.text: āpatsu ca mahāśailaśilāsaṅghātakarkaśam ||
children.translated_text: and in misfortune it is hard as a mass of rock from a great mountain.

children.text: saṃtaptāyasi saṃsthitasya payaso nāmāpi na jñāyate muktākāratayā tad eva nalinīpatrasthitaṃ rājate
children.translated_text: When a drop of water rests on heated iron, even its name is not known; that very same drop, resting on a lotus leaf, shines with the form of a pearl;

children.text: svātyāṃ sāgaraśuktimadhyapatitaṃ tanmauktikaṃ jāyate prāyeṇādhamamadhyamottamaguṇaḥ saṃsargato jāyate ||
children.translated_text: and when it falls into the middle of an ocean shell under <s>Svāti</s>, it becomes a pearl. Generally, low, middling, and excellent qualities arise from association.

children.text: prīṇāti yaḥ sucaritaiḥ pitaraṃ sa putro yad bhartur eva hitam icchati tat kalatram
children.translated_text: He who pleases his father by good conduct is a son; she who desires only her husband's welfare is a wife;

children.text: tan mitram āpadi sukhe ca samakriyaṃ yad etat trayaṃ jagati puṇyakṛto labhante ||
children.translated_text: and that which acts the same in adversity and in happiness is a friend: these three are obtained in the world by those who have done merit.

children.text: eko devaḥ keśavo vā śivo vā hyekaṃ mitraṃ bhūpatir vā yatir vā
children.translated_text: One god, whether <s>Keśava</s> or <s>Śiva</s>; one friend, whether a king or an ascetic;

children.text: eko vāsaḥ pattane vā vane vā hy ekā bhāryā sundarī vā darī vā ||
children.translated_text: one dwelling, whether in a city or in a forest; one wife, whether a beauty or a cave.

children.text: namratvenonnamantaḥ paraguṇakathanaiḥ svān guṇān khyāpayantaḥ svārthān sampādayanto vitatapṛthutarārambhayatnāḥ parārthe
children.translated_text: Rising high through humility, proclaiming their own virtues by speaking of the virtues of others, accomplishing their own aims through the broad and expansive efforts they undertake for others' sake,

children.text: kṣāntyaivākṣeparukṣākṣaramukharamukhān durjanān dūṣayantaḥ santaḥ sāścaryacaryā jagati bahumatāḥ kasya nābhyarcanīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by forbearance alone shaming wicked people whose mouths are noisy with harsh words of abuse: good people, whose conduct is wondrous, are honored in the world; who would not worship them?

children.text: bhavanti namrās taravaḥ phalodgamairnavāmbubhir dūrāvalambino ghanāḥ
children.translated_text: Trees become bent down by the growth of fruit; clouds hang low with fresh water;

children.text: anuddhatāḥ satpuruṣāḥ samṛddhibhiḥ svabhāva eṣa paropakāriṇām ||
children.translated_text: good people are not haughty through prosperity: this is the nature of those who benefit others.

children.text: śrotraṃ śrutenaiva na kuṇḍalena dānena pāṇir na tu kaṅkaṇena
children.translated_text: The ear shines by learning alone, not by an earring; the hand by giving, not by a bracelet;

children.text: vibhāti kāyaḥ karuṇaparāṇāṃ paropakārair na tu candanena ||
children.translated_text: the body of those devoted to compassion shines by acts of help for others, not by sandal paste.

children.text: pāpān nivārayati yojayate hitāya guhyaṃ nigūhati guṇān prakaṭīkaroti
children.translated_text: It restrains from sins and joins one to what is beneficial; it conceals secrets and makes virtues manifest;

children.text: āpadgataṃ ca na jahāti dadāti kāle sanmitralakṣaṇam idaṃ pravadanti santaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it does not abandon one who has fallen into misfortune, and it gives at the proper time: good people declare this to be the mark of a true friend.

children.text: padmākaraṃ dinakaro vikacīkaroti camdrp volāsayati kairavacakravālam
children.translated_text: The sun makes the lotus-pond open; the moon makes the whole circle of night-lotuses bloom;

children.text: nābhyarthito jaladharo 'pi jalaṃ dadāti santaḥ svayaṃ parahite vihitābhiyogāḥ ||
children.translated_text: even the rain-cloud gives water without being asked. Good people are, of themselves, intent on the welfare of others.

children.text: eke satpuruṣāḥ parārthaghaṭakāḥ svārthaṃ parityajanti ye sāmānyās tu parārtham udyamabhṛtaḥ svārthāvirodhena ye
children.translated_text: Some good people, producers of others' welfare, abandon their own interest; but ordinary people are those who undertake effort for another's sake when it does not conflict with their own interest.

children.text: te 'mī mānuṣarākṣasāḥ parahitaṃ svārthāya nighnanti ye ye tu ghnanti nirarthakaṃ parahitaṃ te ke na jānīmahe ||
children.translated_text: Those who destroy another's welfare for the sake of their own interest are human demons. But those who destroy another's welfare for no purpose: what they are, we do not know.

children.text: kṣīreṇātmagatodakāya hi guṇā dattā purā te 'khilā kṣīrottāpam avekṣya tena payasā svātmā kṛśānau hutaḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago all those qualities were given by milk to the water that had entered into itself; seeing the heating of the milk, that water cast itself into the fire.

children.text: gantuṃ pāvakam unmanas tad abhavad dṛṣṭvā tu mitrāpadaṃ yuktaṃ tena jalena śāmyati satāṃ maitrī punas tv īdṛśī ||
children.translated_text: When the milk, distressed, was about to go into the fire on seeing its friend's danger, then it was proper that it was calmed by that water. Such indeed is the friendship of good people.

children.text: itaḥ svapiti keśavaḥ kulam itas tadīyadviṣām itaś ca śaraṇārthināṃ śikhariṇāṃ gaṇāḥ śerate
children.translated_text: On this side <s>Keśava</s> sleeps; on that side is the clan of his enemies; on another side lie groups of mountains seeking refuge;

children.text: ito 'pi baḍavānalaḥ saha samastasaṃvartakair aho vitatam ūrjitaṃ bharasahaṃ sindhor vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and on this side too is the submarine fire together with all the fires of universal destruction. Ah, vast, mighty, and able to bear burdens is the body of the ocean.

children.text: tṛṣṇāṃ chinddhi bhaja kṣamāṃ jahi madaṃ pāpe ratiṃ mā kṛthāḥ satyaṃ brūhy anuyāhi sādhupadavīṃ sevasva vidvajjanam
children.translated_text: Cut off craving; cultivate patience; abandon pride; do not take delight in sin; speak truth; follow the path of the good; serve learned people;

children.text: mānyān mānaya vidviṣo 'py anunaya prakhyāpaya praśrayaṃ kīrtiṃ pālaya duḥkhite kuru dayām etat satāṃ ceṣṭitam ||
children.translated_text: honor those worthy of honor; conciliate even enemies; make humility known; preserve your fame; show compassion to the suffering: this is the conduct of good people.

children.text: manasi vacasi kāye puṇyapīyūṣapūrṇāstribhuvanam upakāraśreṇibhiḥ prīṇayantaḥ
children.translated_text: Filled in mind, speech, and body with the nectar of merit, delighting the three worlds with rows of benefits,

children.text: paraguṇaparamāṇūn parvatīkṛtya nityaṃ nijahṛdi vikasantaḥ santaḥ santaḥ kiyantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and always making the minute atoms of others' virtues into mountains while blooming in their own hearts: how many good people, truly good people, are there?

children.text: kiṃ tena hemagiriṇā rajatādriṇā vā yatrāśritāś ca taravas taravas ta eva
children.translated_text: What use is that golden mountain, or that silver mountain, where the trees that have taken refuge are simply trees as before?

children.text: manyāmahe malayam eva yadāśrayeṇa kaṅkolanimbakaṭujā api candanāḥ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: We regard only <s>Malaya</s> as worthy, by taking refuge in which even kaṅkola, neem, and bitter-born trees become sandalwood.

children.text: ratnair mahārhais tutuṣur na devā na bhejire bhīmaviṣeṇa bhītim
children.translated_text: The gods were not satisfied with very costly jewels, nor did they give way to fear because of the dreadful poison;

children.text: sudhāṃ vinā na paryayur virāmaṃ na niścitārthād viramanti dhīrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: without nectar they did not come to rest. The steadfast do not turn back from a purpose that has been firmly resolved.

children.text: kvacit pṛthvīśayyaḥ kvacid api ca paryaṅkaśayanaḥ kvacicchākāhāraḥ kvacid api ca śālyodanaruciḥ
children.translated_text: At one time he may have the earth as his bed; at another, he may sleep on a couch. At one time he may eat vegetables; at another, he may enjoy rice cooked from fine grain.

children.text: kvacit kanthādhārī kvacid api ca divyāmbaradharo manasvī kāryārthī na gaṇayati duḥkhaṃ na ca sukham ||
children.translated_text: At one time he may wear a patched cloak; at another, he may wear divine garments. A high-minded person intent on his task counts neither pain nor pleasure.

children.text: aiśvaryasya vibhūṣaṇaṃ sujanatā śauryasya vāksaṃyamo jñānasyopaśamaḥ śrutasya vinayo vittasya pātre vyayaḥ
children.translated_text: Goodness is the ornament of sovereignty; restraint of speech, of valor; calmness, of knowledge; humility, of learning; expenditure on a worthy recipient, of wealth;

children.text: akrodhas tapasaḥ kṣamā prabhavitur dharmasya nirvājatā sarveṣām api sarvakāraṇam idaṃ śīlaṃ paraṃ bhūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: freedom from anger, of asceticism; forgiveness, of power; sincerity, of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order). This character, the supreme ornament, is the cause of all these in everyone.

children.text: nindantu nītinipuṇā yadi vā stuvantu lakṣmīḥ samāviśatu gacchatu vā yatheṣṭam
children.translated_text: Let those skilled in ethics either censure or praise; let <s>Lakṣmī</s> enter in or go away as she pleases.

children.text: adyaiva vā maraṇam astu yugāntare vā nyāyyāt pathaḥ pravicalanti padaṃ na dhīrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let death come this very day or in another age: the steadfast do not move even a step from the path of justice.

children.text: bhagnāśasya karaṇḍapiṇḍitatanor mlānendriyasya kṣudhā kṛtvākhur vivaraṃ svayaṃ nipatito naktaṃ mukhe bhoginaḥ
children.translated_text: A mouse, its hopes broken, its body confined in a basket, its senses faint from hunger, made a hole and at night fell of itself into the mouth of a serpent.

children.text: tṛptas tatpiśitena satvaram asau tenaiva yātaḥ yathā lokāḥ paśyata daivam eva hi nṛṇāṃ vṛddhau kṣaye kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Satisfied with its flesh, that serpent quickly departed by that very opening. See, people: fate alone is the cause of men's prosperity and decline.

children.text: ālasyaṃ hi manuṣyāṇāṃ śarīrastho mahān ripuḥ
children.translated_text: For human beings, idleness is a great enemy lodged in the body.

children.text: nāsty udyamasamo bandhuḥ kurvāṇo nāvasīdati ||
children.translated_text: There is no kinsman equal to effort; one who acts does not sink down.

children.text: chinno 'pi rohati taruḥ kṣīṇo 'py upacīyate punaś candraḥ
children.translated_text: Even when cut, a tree grows again; even when diminished, the moon again waxes.

children.text: iti vimṛśantaḥ santaḥ saṃtapyante na duḥkheṣu ||
children.translated_text: Reflecting thus, the good do not torment themselves amid sorrows.

children.text: netā yasya bṛhaspatiḥ praharaṇaṃ vajraṃ surāḥ sainikāḥ svargo durgam anugrahaḥ kila harer airāvato vāraṇaḥ
children.translated_text: He whose leader is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, whose weapon is the thunderbolt, whose soldiers are the gods, whose fortress is heaven, whose favor indeed is <s>Hari</s>'s, and whose elephant is <s>Airāvata</s>,

children.text: ity aiśvaryabalānvito 'pi balabhid bhagnaḥ paraiḥ saṅgare tad vyaktaṃ nanu daivam eva śaraṇaṃ dhig dhig vṛthā pauruṣam ||
children.translated_text: even <s>Balabhid</s>, endowed with such lordship and strength, was defeated by enemies in battle. Therefore it is plainly fate alone that is refuge; shame, shame on vain manly effort.

children.text: karmāyattaṃ phalaṃ puṃsāṃ buddhiḥ karmānusāriṇī
children.translated_text: The fruit of men depends on action; intellect follows action.

children.text: tathāpi sudhiyā bhāvyaṃ suvicāryaiva kurvatā ||
children.translated_text: Even so, an intelligent person should act only after careful consideration.

children.text: khalvāṭo divaseśvarasya kiraṇaiḥ saṃtāḍito mastake vāñchan deśam anātapaṃ vidhivaśāt tālasya mūlaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: A bald man, struck on the head by the rays of the lord of day and desiring a place without heat, went by force of fate to the foot of a palm tree.

children.text: tatrāpy asya mahāphalena patatā bhagnaṃ saśabdaṃ śiraḥ prāyo gacchati yatra bhāgyarahitas tatraiva yānty āpadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too his head was loudly broken by a great fruit falling on him. Usually, wherever a luckless man goes, there calamities themselves go.

children.text: raviniśākarayor grahapīḍanaṃ gajabhujaṅgamayor api bandhanam
children.translated_text: Seeing the eclipsing affliction of the sun and moon, the bondage even of elephant and serpent,

children.text: matimatāṃ ca vilokya daridratāṃ vidhir aho balavān iti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the poverty of the wise, my thought is this: ah, destiny is powerful.

children.text: sṛjati tāvad aśeṣaguṇakaraṃ puruṣaratnam alaṃkaraṇaṃ bhuvaḥ
children.translated_text: Destiny first creates a jewel among men, a maker of every virtue, an ornament of the earth.

children.text: tad api tatkṣaṇabhaṅgi karoti ced ahaha kaṣṭam apaṇḍitatā vidheḥ ||
children.translated_text: Yet if it makes him perish in that very moment, ah, how painful is the ignorance of destiny.

children.text: patraṃ naiva yadā karīraviṭape doṣo vasantasya kim nolūko 'py avalokate yadi divā sūryasya kiṃ dūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: When there is no leaf on the branch of the <s>karīra</s> tree, what fault is spring's? If the owl does not see by day, what blame is the sun's?

children.text: dhārā naiva patanti cātakamukhe meghasya kiṃ dūṣaṇam yat pūrvaṃ vidhinā lalāṭalikhitaṃ tan mārjituṃ kaḥ kṣamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If streams of rain do not fall into the <s>cātaka</s>'s mouth, what fault is the cloud's? Who is able to erase what was formerly written by destiny on the forehead?

children.text: namasyāmo devān nanu hatavidhes te 'pi vaśagā vidhir vandyaḥ so 'pi pratiniyatakarmaikaphaladaḥ
children.translated_text: We bow to the gods; yet surely they too are subject to ruined fate. Fate is to be worshipped; yet it too gives only the single fruit of fixed action.

children.text: phalaṃ karmāyattaṃ yadi kim amaraiḥ kiṃ ca vidhinā namas tatkarmabhyo vidhir api na yebhyaḥ prabhavati ||
children.translated_text: If the fruit depends on action, what use are the immortals, and what use is fate? Homage to those actions over which even fate has no power.

children.text: brahmā yena kulālavan niyamito brahmāṇḍabhāṇḍodare viṣṇur yena daśāvatāragahane kṣipto mahāsaṅkaṭe
children.translated_text: By that which has constrained <s>Brahmā</s> like a potter within the vessel-belly of the cosmic egg, and by which <s>Viṣṇu</s> has been thrown into the great distress of the difficult ten incarnations,

children.text: rudro yena kapālapāṇipuṭake bhikṣāṭanaṃ kāritaḥ sūryo bhrāmyati nityam eva gagane tasmai namaḥ karmaṇe ||
children.translated_text: by which <s>Rudra</s> has been made to wander for alms with a skull in his cupped hands, and by which the sun continually roams in the sky: homage to that <s>karma</s> (action).

children.text: naivākṛtiḥ phalati naiva kulaṃ na śīlaṃ vidyāpi naiva na ca yatnakṛtāpi sevā
children.translated_text: Neither appearance bears fruit, nor birth, nor conduct; neither learning nor even service performed with effort bears fruit.

children.text: bhāgyāni pūrvatapasā khalu saṃcitāni kāle phalanti puruṣasya yathaiva vṛkṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fortunes, truly accumulated by former austerity, bear fruit for a man in due time, just like trees.

children.text: vane raṇe śatrujalāgnimadhye mahārṇave parvatamastake vā
children.translated_text: In a forest, in battle, amid enemies, water, and fire, in the great ocean or on a mountain peak,

children.text: suptaṃ pramattaṃ viṣamasthitaṃ vā rakṣanti puṇyāni purākṛtāni ||
children.translated_text: whether asleep, negligent, or placed in danger, the meritorious deeds done before protect one.

children.text: yā sādhūṃś ca khalān karoti viduṣo mūrkhān hitān dveṣiṇaḥ pratyakṣaṃ kurute parīkṣam amṛtaṃ hālāhalaṃ tatkṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: That blessed good conduct, which makes the good and the wicked, the learned and fools, friends and enemies, and in an instant turns what is visibly poison into nectar and <s>hālāhala</s> poison,

children.text: tām ārādhaya satkriyāṃ bhagavatīṃ bhoktuṃ phalaṃ vāñchitaṃ he sādho vyasanair guṇeṣu vipuleṣv āsthāṃ vṛthā mā kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: worship her, O good man, if you desire to enjoy the wished-for fruit. Do not place your trust vainly in the calamities that attend abundant virtues.

children.text: guṇavad aguṇavad vā kurvatā kāryajātaṃ pariṇatir avadhāryā yatnataḥ paṇḍitena
children.translated_text: Whether he performs a task with virtue or without virtue, the learned man must carefully ascertain the outcome.

children.text: atirabhasakṛtānāṃ karmaṇām ā vipatterbhavati hṛdayadāhī śalyatulyo vipākaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For deeds done with excessive haste have a result, extending to disaster, that burns the heart like a thorn.

children.text: sthālyāṃ vaidūryamayyāṃ pacati tilakaṇāṃś candanair indhanaughaiḥ sauvarṇair lāṅgalāgrair vilikhati vasudhām arkamūlasya hetoḥ
children.translated_text: He cooks sesame grains in a vessel made of beryl, with heaps of sandalwood as fuel; he ploughs the earth with golden ploughshares for the sake of the root of the arka plant.

children.text: kṛtvā karpūrakhaṇḍān vṛttim iha kurute kodravāṇāṃ samantātprāpyemāṃ karmabhūmiṃ na carati manujo yas topa mandabhāgyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made pieces of camphor, he uses them here as a livelihood all around for kodrava grain: the unfortunate man who has obtained this land of action and does not act is just such a fool.

children.text: majjatv ambhasi yātu meruśikharaṃ śatruṃ jayatvāhave vāṇijyaṃ kṛṣisevane ca sakalā vidyāḥ kalāḥ śikṣatām
children.translated_text: Let him plunge into water, go to the summit of <s>Meru</s>, conquer an enemy in battle, learn trade, agriculture, service, and all sciences and arts.

children.text: ākāśaṃ vipulaṃ prayātu khagavat kṛtvā prayatnaṃ paraṃ nābhāvyaṃ bhavatīha karmavaśato bhāvyasya nāśaḥ kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let him, like a bird, range through the wide sky after making the utmost effort: what is not destined does not come to be here through the force of karma; and how could what is destined be destroyed?

children.text: bhīmaṃ vanaṃ bhavati tasya puraṃ pradhānaṃ sarvo janaḥ svajanatām upayāti tasya
children.translated_text: For the man who has abundant past merit, a fearsome forest becomes a chief city, and every person comes to be like his own kinsman.

children.text: kṛtsnā ca bhūr bhavati sannidhiratnapūrṇā yasyāsti pūrvasukṛtaṃ vipulaṃ narasya ||
children.translated_text: The whole earth becomes for him a treasure-house filled with jewels close at hand.

children.text: ko lābho guṇisaṅgamaḥ kim asukhaṃ prājñetaraiḥ saṅgatiḥ kā hāniḥ samayacyutir nipuṇatā kā dharmatattve ratiḥ
children.translated_text: What is gain? Association with the virtuous. What is unhappiness? Association with those other than the wise. What is loss? Missing the right time. What is skill? Delight in the truth of <s>dharma</s> (normative order).

children.text: kaḥ śūro vijitendriyaḥ priyatamā kānuvratā kiṃ dhanaṃ vidyā kiṃ sukham apravāsagamanaṃ rājyaṃ kim ājñāphalam ||
children.translated_text: Who is brave? One who has conquered his senses. Who is the dearest wife? One who is faithful. What is wealth? Learning. What is happiness? Not going abroad. What is kingship? The fruit of command.

children.text: apriyavacanadaridraiḥ priyavacanadhanāḍhyaiḥ svadāraparituṣṭaiḥ
children.translated_text: With people poor in unpleasant speech, rich in pleasant speech, content with their own wives,

children.text: paraparivādanivṛttaiḥ kvacit kvacin maṇḍitā vasudhā ||
children.translated_text: and turned away from slandering others, the earth is adorned here and there, in a few places.

children.text: kadarthitasyāpi hi dhairyavṛtterna śakyate dhairyaguṇaḥ pramārṣṭum
children.translated_text: Even when a man of steadfast conduct has been mistreated, the quality of his steadfastness cannot be wiped away;

children.text: adhomukhasyāpi kṛtasya vahnernādhaḥ śikhā yāti kadācid eva ||
children.translated_text: for even when fire has been made to face downward, its flame never goes downward.

children.text: kāntākaṭākṣaviśikhā na lunanti yasya cittaṃ na nirdahati kipakṛśānutāpaḥ
children.translated_text: The man whose mind the arrow-like glances of a beloved woman do not cut, whom the burning heat of anger does not scorch,

children.text: karṣanti bhūriviṣayāś ca na lobhapāśairlokatrayaṃ jayati kṛtsnam idaṃ sa dhīraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whom abundant sense-objects do not drag along with the nooses of greed, that steadfast man conquers this entire triple world.

children.text: ekenāpi hi śūreṇa pādākrāntaṃ mahītalam
children.translated_text: Even by one hero alone the surface of the earth is trodden underfoot,

children.text: kriyate bhāskareṇaiva sphārasphuritatejasā ||
children.translated_text: just as it is by the sun alone, with its widely flashing splendor.

children.text: vahnis tasya jalāyate jalanidhiḥ kulyāyate tatkṣaṇānmeruḥ svalpaśilāyate mṛgapatiḥ sadyaḥ kuraṅgāyate
children.translated_text: Fire becomes water for him; the ocean at once becomes a little canal; <s>Meru</s> becomes a small stone; the lord of beasts immediately becomes a deer;

children.text: vyālo mālyaguṇāyate viṣarasaḥ pīyūṣavarṣāyate yasyāṅge 'khilalokavallabhatamaṃ śīlaṃ samunmīlati ||
children.translated_text: a serpent becomes a garland-string; the taste of poison becomes a shower of nectar, when character, most beloved to the whole world, unfolds in a person's body.

children.text: lajjāguṇaughajananīṃ jananīm iva svāmatyantaśuddhahṛdayām anuvartamānām
children.translated_text: Following his own mother, as it were, the mother of a flood of the virtues of modesty, whose heart is utterly pure,

children.text: tejasvinaḥ sukham asūn api saṃtyajanti satyavratavyasanino na punaḥ pratijñām ||
children.translated_text: men of spirit gladly abandon even their lives when devoted to the vow of truth, but they do not abandon their promise.

children.text: Chapter 2
śambhusvayambhuharayo hariṇekṣaṇānāṃ yenākriyanta satataṃ gṛhakumbhadāsāḥ
children.translated_text: By whom <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Svayambhū</s>, and <s>Hari</s> were constantly made household pot-slaves of doe-eyed women,

children.text: vācām agocaracaritravicitritāya tasmai namo bhagavate makaradhvajāya ||
children.translated_text: to that blessed <s>Makaradhvaja</s>, whose conduct is made wondrous beyond the reach of words, homage.

children.text: smitena bhāvena ca lajjayā bhiyā parāṅmukhair ardhakaṭākṣavīkṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: With a smile, with feeling, with modesty, with fear, with half-sidelong glances from averted faces,

children.text: vacobhir īrṣyākalahena līlayā samastabhāvaiḥ khalu bandhanaṃ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with words, with jealous quarrel, with play: with all their gestures, women are indeed a bondage.

children.text: bhrūcāturyāt kuṣcitākṣāḥ kaṭākṣāḥ snigdhā vāco lajjitāntāś ca hāsāḥ
children.translated_text: Glances made charming by the eyebrows, eyes somewhat contracted, affectionate words, and smiles ending in modesty,

children.text: līlāmandaṃ prasthitaṃ ca sthitaṃ ca strīṇām etad bhūṣaṇaṃ cāyudhaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: a playful slow going forth and standing still: this is both the ornament and the weapon of women.

children.text: kvacit sabhrūbhaṅgaiḥ kvacid api ca lajjāparigataiḥ kvacid bhūritrastaiḥ kvacid api ca līlāvilalitaiḥ
children.translated_text: In some places with bends of the eyebrows, in some places enveloped in modesty, in some places very frightened, and in some places playfully graceful,

children.text: kumārīṇām etair madanasubhagair netravalitaiḥ sphurannīlābjānāṃ prakaraparikīrṇā iva diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by these love-beautified turnings of maidens' eyes, the directions seem as if strewn with clusters of flashing blue lotuses.

children.text: vaktraṃ candravikāsi paṅkajaparīhāsakṣame locane varṇaḥ svarṇam apākariṣṇur alinījiṣṇuḥ kacānāṃ cayaḥ
children.translated_text: A face blooming like the moon, eyes capable of mocking lotuses, a complexion that robs gold of its pride, a mass of hair conquering swarms of bees,

children.text: vakṣojāvibhakumbhavibhramaharau gurvī nitambasthalī vācāṃ hāri ca mārdavaṃ yuvatīṣu svābhāvikaṃ maṇḍanam ||
children.translated_text: breasts stealing the charm of elephant frontal globes, a weighty expanse of hips, and a captivating softness of speech: among young women this is their natural adornment.

children.text: smitakiṃcinmugdhaṃ saralataralo dṛṣṭivibhavaḥ parispando vācām abhinavavilāsoktisarasaḥ
children.translated_text: A smile somewhat innocent in its charm, the wealth of a gaze straightforward and tremulous, the quiver of speech juicy with newly playful utterance,

children.text: gatānām ārambhaḥ kisalayitalīlāparikaraḥ spṛśantyās tāruṇyaṃ kim iva na hi ramyaṃ mṛgadṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the beginning of movements with an equipment of sprouting playfulness: as a doe-eyed woman touches youth, what is not lovely?

children.text: draṣṭavyeṣu kim uttamaṃ mṛgadṛśaḥ premaprasannaṃ mukhaṃ ghrātavyeṣv api kiṃ tadāsyapavanaḥ śravyeṣu kiṃ tadvacaḥ
children.translated_text: Among things to be seen, what is best? The love-bright face of a doe-eyed woman. Among things to be smelled, what? The breath of her mouth. Among things to be heard, what? Her speech.

children.text: kiṃ svādyeṣu tadoṣṭhapallavarasaḥ spṛśyeṣu kiṃ tadvapurdhyeyaṃ kiṃ navayauvane sahṛdayaiḥ sarvatra tadvibhramāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among things to be tasted, what? The sap of her leaf-like lips. Among things to be touched, what? Her body. What is to be meditated on by sensitive men in fresh youth? Her graces everywhere.

children.text: etāś caladvalayasaṃhatimekhalotthajhaṅkāranūpuraparājitarājahaṃsyaḥ
children.translated_text: These young women, whose tinkling anklets defeat royal swans, with jingling rising from girdles made of clusters of moving bracelets,

children.text: kurvanti kasya na mano vivaśaṃ taruṇyo vitrastamugdhahariṇīsadṛśaiḥ kaṭākṣaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose sidelong glances are like frightened, innocent fawns, whose mind do they not make helpless?

children.text: kuṅkumapaṅkakalaṅkitadehā gaurapayodharakampitahārā
children.translated_text: Her body is stained with a smear of saffron, her necklace trembles on her fair breasts,

children.text: nūpurahaṃsaraṇatpadmā kaṃ na vaśīkurute bhuvi rāmā ||
children.translated_text: her anklets make swan-like sounds at her lotus feet: whom on earth does such a lovely woman not bring under her power?

children.text: nūnaṃ hi te kavivarā viparītavāco ye nityam āhur abalā iti kāminīs tāḥ
children.translated_text: Surely those best of poets who constantly call passionate women 'weak' speak perversely;

children.text: yābhir vilolitaratārakadṛṣṭipātaiḥ śakrādayo 'pi vijitās tv abalāḥ kathaṃ tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: when even <s>Śakra</s> and the others have been conquered by the glances of their rolling, starry eyes, how can they be weak?

children.text: nūnam ājñākaras tasyāḥ subhruvo makaradhvajaḥ
children.translated_text: Surely <s>Makaradhvaja</s> acts at the command of that fair-browed woman,

children.text: yatas tannetrasañcārasūciteṣu pravartate ||
children.translated_text: since he proceeds wherever the movements of her eyes indicate.

children.text: keśāḥ saṃyaminaḥ śruter api paraṃ pāraṃ gate locane antarvaktram api svabhāvaśucibhīḥ kīrṇaṃ dvijānāṃ gaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Her hair is restrained; her eyes have gone beyond even the far shore of scripture; even the inside of her mouth is filled with rows of twice-born teeth, naturally pure;

children.text: muktānāṃ satatādhivāsarucirau vakṣojakumbhāv imāvitthaṃ tanvi vapuḥ praśāntam api te rāgaṃ karoty eva naḥ ||
children.translated_text: these pitcher-like breasts are lovely with the constant dwelling of pearls. Thus, slender woman, even though your body is tranquil, it still arouses passion in us.

children.text: mugdhe dhānuṣkatā keyam apūrvā tvayi dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Innocent girl, what is this unprecedented archery seen in you,

children.text: yayā vidhyasi cetāṃsi guṇair eva na sāyakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: by which you pierce hearts with strings of virtues alone, not with arrows?

children.text: sati pradīpe saty agnau satsu tārāravīnduṣu
children.translated_text: Though there is a lamp, though there is fire, though there are stars, the sun, and the moon,

children.text: vinā me mṛgaśāvākṣyā tamobhūtam idaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: without my fawn-eyed woman, this world has become darkness for me.

children.text: udvṛttaḥ stanabhāra eṣa tarale netre cale bhrūlate rāgādhiṣṭhitam oṣṭhapallavam idaṃ kurvantu nāma vyathām
children.translated_text: Let this haughty weight of breasts, these tremulous eyes, these moving creeper-like eyebrows, and this leaf-like lower lip occupied by passion cause pain, if they will;

children.text: saubhāgyākṣaramālikeva likhitā puṣpāyudhena svayaṃ madhyasthāpi karoti tāpam adhikaṃ romāvaliḥ kena sā ||
children.translated_text: but why does that row of body hair, though standing in the middle, cause greater heat, as if it were a garland of letters of good fortune written by the flower-weaponed god himself?

children.text: mukhena candrakāntena mahānīlaiḥ śiroruhaiḥ
children.translated_text: With a face like moonstone, with hair like great sapphires,

children.text: karābhyāṃ padmarāgābhyāṃ reje ratnamayīva sā ||
children.translated_text: and with hands like rubies, she shone as if made of jewels.

children.text: guruṇā stanabhāreṇa mukhacandreṇa bhāsvatā
children.translated_text: With the heavy weight of her breasts, with her shining moon-face,

children.text: śanaiścarābhyāṃ pādābhyāṃ reje grahamayīva sā ||
children.translated_text: and with her two feet like <s>Śanaiścara</s>, she shone as if made of planets.

children.text: tasyāḥ stanau yadi ghanau jaghanaṃ ca hāri vaktraṃ ca cāru tava citte kim ākulatvam
children.translated_text: If her breasts are full, her hips charming, and her face beautiful, why is there agitation in your mind

children.text: puṇyaṃ kuruṣva yadi teṣu tavāsti vāñchā puṇyair vinā na hi bhavanti samīhitārthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Perform merit, if you have any desire for them; without merits, desired ends do not come about.

children.text: ime tāruṇyaśrīnavaparimalāḥ prauḍhasuratapratāpaprārambhāḥ smaravijayadānapratibhuvaḥ
children.translated_text: These fresh fragrances of the splendor of youth, these beginnings of the prowess of mature love-making, these pledges guaranteeing the victory-gift of <s>Smara</s>,

children.text: ciraṃ cetaś corā abhinavavikāraikaguravo vilāsavyāpārāḥ kim api vijayante mṛgadṛśām ||
children.translated_text: these charming operations of doe-eyed women, long-time thieves of the mind and sole teachers of ever-new transformations, somehow triumph.

children.text: praṇayamadhurāḥ premodgārā rasāśrayatāṃ gatāḥ phaṇitimadhurā mugdhaprāyāḥ prakāśitasammadāḥ
children.translated_text: Sweet with affection, outpourings of love, having become abodes of rasa, sweet in speech, mostly innocent, revealing their delight,

children.text: prakṛtisubhagā visrambhārdrāḥ smarodayadāyinī rahasi kim api svairālāpā haranti mṛgīdṛśām ||
children.translated_text: naturally lovely, moist with confidence, bringing on the rise of <s>Smara</s>, the somehow free private conversations of doe-eyed women steal the heart.

children.text: viśramya viśramya vanadrumāṇāṃ chāyāsu tanvī vicacāra kācit
children.translated_text: Pausing again and again in the shade of the forest trees, a certain slender woman wandered about,

children.text: stanottarīyeṇa karoddhṛtena nivārayantī śaśino mayūkhān ||
children.translated_text: warding off the moon's rays with the upper garment over her breasts, lifted by her hand.

children.text: adarśane darśanamātrakāmā dṛṣṭvā pariṣvaṅgasukhaikalolā
children.translated_text: When she is unseen, we desire only the sight of her; having seen her, we are restless only for the pleasure of embrace;

children.text: āliṅgitāyāṃ punar āyatākṣyāmāśāsmahe vigrahayor abhedam ||
children.translated_text: and when the long-eyed woman has been embraced, we hope for the non-difference of the two bodies.

children.text: mālatī śirasi jṛmbhaṇaṃ mukhe candanaṃ vapuṣi kuṅkumāvilam
children.translated_text: Jasmine on the head, a yawn on the face, sandal on the body mingled with saffron,

children.text: vakṣasi priyatamā madālasā svarga eṣa pariśiṣṭa āgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the beloved woman, languid with passion, on the breast: this is the remaining doctrine about heaven.

children.text: prāṅ mām eti manāg anāgatarasaṃ jātābhilāṣāṃ tataḥ savrīḍaṃ tad anu ślathodyamam atha pradhvastadhairyaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: At first she comes to me, with passion not yet quite arrived but desire already born; then she is bashful, after that slack in effort, and then again with courage overthrown;

children.text: premārdraṃ spṛhaṇīyanirbhararahaḥ krīḍāpragalbhaṃ tato niḥsaṅgāṅgavikarṣaṇādhikasukharamyaṃ kulastrīratam ||
children.translated_text: then moist with love, bold in enviable and full secret play, and finally lovely with the greater pleasure of unrestrained drawing of limb against limb: such is the love-making of a woman of good family.

children.text: urasi nipatitānāṃ srastadhammillakānāṃ mukulitanayanānāṃ kiṃcidunmīlitānām
children.translated_text: Of women who have fallen upon the chest, whose hair-knots have slipped, whose eyes are closed and then slightly opened,

children.text: upari suratakhedasvinnagaṇḍasthalānāmadharamadhu vadhūnāṃ bhāgyavantaḥ pibanti ||
children.translated_text: and whose cheeks above are moist with the fatigue of love-making, the fortunate drink the honey of the lower lip.

children.text: āmīlitanayanānāṃ yaḥ surataraso 'nu saṃvidaṃ bhāti
children.translated_text: That aftertaste of erotic pleasure which shines in awareness for those whose eyes are closed,

children.text: mithunair mitho 'vadhāritamavitatham idam eva kāmanirbarhaṇam ||
children.translated_text: this alone, mutually ascertained by couples, is truly the extinction of desire.

children.text: idam anucitam akramaś ca puṃsāṃ yad iha jarāsvapi manmathā vikārāḥ
children.translated_text: This is improper and out of order for men, that even in old age there are transformations caused by <s>Manmatha</s> here;

children.text: tad api ca na kṛtaṃ nitambinīnāṃ stanapatanāvadhi jīvitaṃ rataṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: and yet, for women with rounded hips, neither life nor love has been made to last only until their breasts fall.

children.translated_text: There is in this world nothing other than wealth, family, mansion, and youth that is a single abode of passion, a cause for obtaining the great sufferings of hundreds of hells, the seed of the arising of delusion, a mass of clouds over the moon of knowledge,

children.text: kandarpasyaikamitraṃ prakaṭitavividhaspaṣṭadoṣaprabandhaṃ loke 'smin na hy arthavrajakulabhavanayauvanād anyad asti ||

children.text: śṛṅgāradrumanīrade prasṛmarakrīḍārasasrotasi pradyumnapriyabāndhave caturavāṅmuktāphalodanvati
children.translated_text: When fresh youth has arrived, a rain-cloud for the tree of erotic love, a spreading stream of the rasa of play, the dear kinsman of <s>Pradyumna</s>, an ocean filled with pearls of clever speech,

children.text: tanvīnetracakorapāvanavidhau saubhāgyalakṣmīnidhau dhanyaḥ ko 'pi na vikriyāṃ kalayati prāpte nave yauvane ||
children.translated_text: a moonlight rite that sanctifies the cakora-birds of slender women's eyes, and a treasury of the Lakṣmī of good fortune, blessed indeed is the rare man who does not undergo alteration.

children.text: saṃsāre 'sminn asāre kunṛpatibhavanadvārasevākalaṅkavyāsaṅgavyastadhairyaṃ katham amaladhiyo mānasaṃ saṃvidadhyuḥ

children.text: yady etāḥ prodyadindudyutinicayabhṛto na syur ambhojanetrāḥ preṅkhatkāñcīkalāpāḥ stanabharavinamanmadhyabhājas taruṇyaḥ ||

children.text: siddhādhyāsitakandare haravṛṣaskandhāvarugṇadrume gaṅgādhautaśilātale himavataḥ sthāne sthite śreyasi

children.text: kaḥ kurvīta śiraḥ praṇāmamalinaṃ mlānaṃ manasvī jano yadvitrastakuraṅgaśāvanayanā na syuḥ smarāstraṃ striyaḥ ||

children.text: saṃsāra tava paryantapadavī na davīyasī
children.translated_text: O <s>saṃsāra</s>, the path to your far shore would not be very distant,

children.text: antarā dustarā na syur yadi te madirekṣaṇām ||
children.translated_text: if there were not, in between, the hard-to-cross glances of wine-eyed women.

children.text: diśa vanahariṇībhyo vaṃśakāṇḍacchavīnāṃ kavalam upalakoṭicchinnamūlaṃ kuśānām
children.translated_text: Give to the forest does a mouthful of kuśa grass, whose roots have been cut by the edge of a stone and whose stalks have the sheen of bamboo,

children.text: śakayuvatikapolāpāṇḍutāmbūlavallīdalam aruṇanakhāgraiḥ pāṭitaṃ vā vadhūbhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or give to brides a leaf of betel creeper, pale like the cheek of a Śaka girl and torn by the red tips of their nails.

children.text: asārāḥ sarve te virativirasāḥ pāpaviṣayā jugupsyantāṃ yad vā nanu sakaladoṣāspadam iti
children.translated_text: Let all those sinful sense-objects be despised as worthless, tasteless because they lack detachment, or rather as the abode of every fault;

children.text: tathāpy etadbhūmau nahi parahitāt puṇyam adhikaṃ na cāsmin saṃsāre kuvalayadṛśo ramyam aparam ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless on this earth there is no merit greater than benefiting others, and in this <s>saṃsāra</s> there is nothing more charming than lotus-eyed women.

children.text: etatkāmaphalo loke yad dvayor ekacittatā
children.translated_text: In the world, this is the fruit of desire: that the two have one mind.

children.text: anyacittakṛte kāme śavayor iva saṅgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When desire is directed toward another mind, the union is like that of two corpses.

children.text: mātsaryam utsārya vicārya kāryamāryāḥ samaryādam idaṃ vadantu
children.translated_text: Let noble men, setting envy aside and considering the matter with proper bounds, say this:

children.text: sevyā nitambāḥ kimu bhūdharāṇāmata smarasmeravilāsinīnām ||
children.translated_text: are the slopes of mountains to be frequented, or the buttocks of women smiling with love and play?

children.text: saṃsāre svapnasāre pariṇatitarale dve gatī paṇḍitānāṃ tattvajñānāmṛtāmbhaḥplavalalitadhiyāṃ yātu kālaḥ kathaṃcit
children.translated_text: In this <s>saṃsāra</s>, whose substance is like a dream and whose outcome is unstable, there are two courses for the learned: for those whose minds are made playful by the raft of the nectar-water of knowledge of reality, let time pass somehow;

children.text: no cen mugdhāṅganānāṃ stanajaghanaghanābhogasambhoginīnāṃ sthūlopasthasthalīṣu sthagitakaratalasparśalīlodyamānām ||
children.translated_text: or else, let it pass among innocent women, enjoying the massive fullness of breasts and hips, while the playful effort of hand-touch is arrested on the broad region of their lap.

children.text: āvāsaḥ kriyatāṃ gaṅge pāpahāriṇi vāriṇi
children.translated_text: Let a dwelling be made in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in water that removes sin,

children.text: stanadvaye taruṇyā vā manohāriṇi hāriṇi ||
children.translated_text: or on the two breasts of a young woman, captivating and adorned with necklaces.

children.text: kim iha bahubhir uktair yuktiśūnyaiḥ pralāpairdvayam iha puruṣāṇāṃ sarvadā sevanīyam
children.translated_text: What is the use here of many statements, of empty prattle devoid of reasoning? In this world two things are always to be pursued by men:

children.text: abhinavamadalīlālālasaṃ sundarīṇāṃ stanabharaparikhinnaṃ yauvanaṃ vā vanaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: either the youth of beautiful women, eager for the play of fresh intoxication and wearied by the weight of their breasts, or else the forest.

children.text: satyaṃ janā vacmi na pakṣapātāllokeṣu saptasvapi tathyam etat
children.translated_text: I speak the truth, people, not from partiality: in all the seven worlds this is a fact.

children.text: nānyan manohāri nitambinībhyo duḥkhaikahetur na ca kaścid anyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nothing is more captivating than broad-hipped women, and there is no other single cause of suffering.

children.text: kāntety utpalalocaneti vipulaśroṇībharety unnamatpīnottuṅgapayodhareti samukhāmbhojeti subhrūr iti
children.translated_text: Seeing a woman and saying, 'She is my beloved, lotus-eyed, heavy with broad hips, with rising, full, lofty breasts, with a face like a lotus, with beautiful brows,'

children.text: dṛṣṭvā mādyati modate 'bhiramate prastauti vidvān api pratyakṣāśucibhastrikāṃ striyam aho mohasya duśceṣṭitam ||
children.translated_text: even a learned man becomes drunk, rejoices, takes pleasure, and praises her, though she is plainly a bag of impurity. Ah, how badly delusion behaves!

children.text: smṛtā bhavati tāpāya dṛṣṭā conmādakāriṇī
children.translated_text: Remembered, she becomes a source of burning pain; seen, she produces madness;

children.text: spṛṣṭā bhavati mohāya sā nāma dayitā katham ||
children.translated_text: touched, she becomes a cause of delusion. How, then, is she called beloved?

children.text: tāvad evāmṛtamayī yāvallocanagocarā
children.translated_text: She is made of nectar only so long as she is within range of the eyes;

children.text: cakṣuṣpathād atītā tu viṣād apy atiricyate ||
children.translated_text: but once she has passed beyond the path of sight, she exceeds even poison.

children.text: nāmṛtaṃ na viṣaṃ kiṃcid etāṃ muktvā nitambinīm
children.translated_text: There is no nectar and no poison at all apart from this broad-hipped woman:

children.text: saivāmṛtalatā raktā viraktā viṣavallarī ||
children.translated_text: when attached, she is a creeper of nectar; when disaffected, she is a poisonous vine.

children.text: āvartaḥ saṃśayānām avinayabhuvanaṃ paṭṭanaṃ sāhasānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ sannidhānaṃ kapaṭaśatamayaṃ kṣetram apratyayānām
children.translated_text: A whirlpool of doubts, a realm of immodesty, a city of rash acts, a storehouse of faults, a field made of a hundred deceits and of distrust,

children.text: svargadvārasya vighno narakapuramukhaṃ sarvamāyākaraṇḍaṃ strīyantraṃ kena sṛṣṭaṃ viṣam amṛtamayaṃ prāṇilokasya pāśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: an obstacle to the gate of heaven, the mouth of the city of hell, a casket of every illusion: by whom was this machine called woman created, poison made of nectar, the snare of the world of living beings?

children.text: no satyena mṛgāṅka eṣa vadanībhūto na cendīvaradvandvaṃ locanatāṃ gataṃ na kanakair apy aṅgayaṣṭiḥ kṛtā
children.translated_text: It is not truly the moon that has become her face, nor has a pair of blue lotuses become her eyes, nor has her slender body been made even from gold.

children.text: kintv evaṃ kavibhiḥ pratāritamanās tattvaṃ vijānann api tvaṅmāṃsāsthimayaṃ vapur mṛgadṛśāṃ mando janaḥ sevate ||
children.translated_text: Yet, though he knows the truth, the dull man, his mind deceived in this way by poets, serves the body of doe-eyed women, made of skin, flesh, and bone.

children.text: līlāvatīnāṃ sahajā vilāsāsta eva mūḍhasya hṛdi sphuranti
children.translated_text: The innate graces of playful women are the very things that flash in the fool's heart.

children.text: rāgo nalinyā hi nisargasiddhastatra bhramatyeva vṛthā ṣaḍaṅghriḥ ||
children.translated_text: For redness is naturally present in the lotus; the six-footed bee merely wanders there in vain.

children.text: saṃmohayanti madayanti viḍambayanti nirbhartsayanti ramayanti viṣādayanti
children.translated_text: They bewilder, intoxicate, mock, rebuke, delight, and sadden.

children.text: etāḥ praviśya sadayaṃ hṛdayaṃ narāṇāṃ kiṃ nāma vāmanayanā na samācaranti ||

children.translated_text: This lotus-face of the slender woman, surpassing the splendor of the full moon and of noble form, in which the honey of the lower lip dwells:

children.translated_text: They chatter with one man, look coquettishly at another,

children.translated_text: In this ocean of existence the fisherman <s>Makara-ketana</s> has spread out a hook called woman,

children.translated_text: In the wilderness of a passionate woman's body, hard to cross because of the mountains of her breasts,

children.translated_text: I have not been seen by that eye, a serpent with long, restless facial movement, brilliant, enjoying itself, and dark as a blue lotus.

children.translated_text: Here there is sweet singing; this is dancing; this is its flavor; that fragrance quivers; this is the touch of breasts.

children.translated_text: It cannot be reached by mantras, nor does it become an object for medicine, nor does it perish through hundreds of various rites of pacification.

children.translated_text: This epilepsy of <s>Smara</s>, repeatedly producing some strange distortion in the body through possession by delusion, makes the gaze whirl and roll.

children.text: jātyandhāya ca durmukhāya ca jarājīrṇākhilāṅgāya ca grāmīṇāya ca duṣkulāya ca galatkuṣṭhābhibhūtāya ca
children.translated_text: To men blind from birth, foul-faced, with all limbs worn out by old age, rustic, of bad family, and overwhelmed by oozing leprosy,

children.translated_text: when courtesans give their charming bodies out of a tiny faith in the beauty of their own form, who would be attached to these courtesans, knives to the wish-granting creeper of discernment?

children.text: veśyāsau madanajvālā rūpendhanavivardhitā
children.translated_text: A courtesan is a flame of passion, increased by the fuel of beauty,

children.text: kāmibhir yatra hūyante yauvanāni dhanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: into which lustful men offer their youth and their wealth.

children.text: kaś cumbati kulapuruṣo veśyādharapallavaṃ manojñam api
children.translated_text: What man of good family would kiss the lovely young leaf of a courtesan's lower lip,

children.text: cārabhaṭacoraceṭakanaṭaviṭaniṣṭhīvanaśarāvam ||
children.translated_text: a spittoon for spies, soldiers, thieves, servants, actors, and libertines?

children.text: dhanyās ta eva dhavalāyatalocanānāṃ tāruṇyadarpaghanapīnapayodharāṇām
