children.translated_text: Blessed indeed are those whose minds do not undergo distortion

children.text: kṣāmodaroparilasattrivalīlatānāṃ dṛṣṭvākṛtiṃ vikṛtim eti mano na yeṣām ||
children.translated_text: when they see the form of women with wide, bright eyes, with firm, full breasts swollen by the pride of youth, and with creeper-like triple folds shining above their slender bellies.

children.text: bāle līlāmukulitam amī mantharā dṛṣṭipātāḥ kiṃ kṣipyante virama virama vyartha eṣa śramas te
children.translated_text: Girl, why are these slow glances, playfully half-closed like buds, being cast? Stop, stop; this effort of yours is useless.

children.text: sampraty anye vayam uparataṃ bālyam āsthā vanānte kṣīṇo mohas tṛṇam iva jagajjālam ālokayāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now we are different men: childhood is past, our attachment is fixed on the forest's edge, delusion has waned, and we look on the net of the world as mere grass.

children.text: iyaṃ bālā māṃ praty anavaratam indīvaradalaprabhā cīraṃ cakṣuḥ kṣipati kim abhipretam anayā
children.translated_text: This girl keeps casting at me an eye whose beauty is like a petal of a blue lotus. What does she intend by this?

children.text: gato moho 'smākaṃ smaraśabarabāṇavyatikarajvarajvālā śāntā tad api na varākī viramati ||
children.translated_text: Our delusion is gone; the burning flames of fever from the contact of <s>Smara</s>'s hunter-like arrows have been quenched. Yet still the poor girl does not desist.

children.text: kiṃ kandarpa karaṃ kadarthayasi re kodaṇḍaṭaṅkāritaṃ re re kokila komalaṃ kalaravaṃ kiṃ vā vṛthā jalpasi
children.translated_text: Why, <s>Kandarpa</s>, do you trouble your hand by twanging your bow? Hey, hey, cuckoo, why do you chatter your soft sweet notes in vain?

children.text: mugdhe snigdhavidagdhacārumadhurair lolaiḥ kaṭākṣair alaṃ cetaś cumbitacandracūḍacaraṇadhyānāmṛtaṃ vartate ||
children.translated_text: Innocent girl, enough of your restless sidelong glances, charming, affectionate, clever, and sweet: my mind abides in the nectar of meditation on the feet of the moon-crested lord.

children.text: virahe 'pi saṅgamaḥ khalu parasparaṃ saṃgataṃ mano yeṣām
children.translated_text: Even in separation there is surely union for those whose minds are joined to one another.

children.text: hṛdayam api vighaṭṭitaṃ cet saṅgī virahaṃ viśeṣayati ||
children.translated_text: But if the heart too is torn apart, then even one who is together intensifies separation.

children.text: kiṃ gatena yadi sā na jīvati prāṇiti priyatamā tathāpi kim
children.translated_text: What use is going home if she is not alive? And even if my beloved lives, what then?

children.text: ity udīkṣya navameghamālikāṃ na prayāti pathikaḥ svamandiram ||
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, after gazing at the line of fresh clouds, the traveler does not go to his own house.

children.text: viramata budhā yoṣitsaṅgāt sukhāt kṣaṇabhaṅgurāt kuruta karuṇāmaitrīprajñāvadhūjanasaṅgamam
children.translated_text: Cease, wise men, from the company of women, a pleasure broken in a moment; seek instead the company of the brides called compassion, friendship, and wisdom.

children.text: na khalu narake hārākrāntaṃ ghanastanamaṇḍalaṃ śaraṇam athavā śroṇībimbaṃ raṇanmaṇimekhalam ||
children.translated_text: For in hell there is certainly no refuge in a dense circle of breasts pressed by necklaces, nor in the curve of hips with a tinkling jeweled girdle.

children.text: yadā yogābhyāsavyasanakṛśayor ātmamanasoravicchinnā maitrī sphurati kṛtinas tasya kimu taiḥ
children.translated_text: When, for a fortunate man, an unbroken friendship between self and mind, both made lean by devotion to the practice of yoga, begins to shine, what need has he of those things:

children.text: priyāṇām ālāpair adharamadhubhir vaktravidhubhiḥ saniśvāsāmodaiḥ sakucakalaśāśleṣasurataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the conversations of beloved women, the honey of their lips, the moons of their faces, the fragrance of their sighs, or love-play with embraces of their pitcher-like breasts?

children.text: yadāsīd ajñānaṃ smaratimirasañcārajanitaṃ tadā dṛṣṭanārīmayam idam aśeṣaṃ jagad iti
children.translated_text: When there was ignorance, born from the movement of the darkness of passion, then this whole world seemed made entirely of women.

children.text: idānīm asmākaṃ paṭutaravivekāñjanajuṣāṃ samībhūtā dṛṣṭis tribhuvanam api brahma manute ||
children.translated_text: Now, for us whose vision is furnished with the sharper collyrium of discernment, sight has become even, and it regards even the three worlds as <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tāvad eva kṛtinām api sphuratyeṣa nirmalavivekadīpakaḥ
children.translated_text: Only so long does this lamp of stainless discernment shine even for fortunate men,

children.text: yāvad eva na kuraṅgacakṣuṣāṃ tāḍyate caṭulalocanāñcalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: as it is not struck by the restless corners of the eyes of doe-eyed women.

children.text: vacasi bhavati saṅgatyāgam uddiśya vārtā śrutimukharamukhānāṃ kevalaṃ paṇḍitānām
children.translated_text: In the speech of learned men, whose mouths are noisy at the ear, there is only talk aimed at abandoning attachment.

children.text: jaghanam aruṇaratnagranthikāñcīkalāpaṃ kuvalayanayanānāṃ ko vihātuṃ samarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But who is able to abandon the hips of lotus-eyed women, girdled with a belt strung with red jewels?

children.text: svaparapratārako 'sau nindati yo 'līkapaṇḍito yuvatīḥ
children.translated_text: That false scholar deceives himself and others when he censures young women,

children.text: yasmāt tapaso 'pi phalaṃ svargaḥ svarge 'pi cāpsarasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: since even the fruit of austerity is heaven, and in heaven too there are apsarases.

children.text: mattebhakumbhadalane bhuvi santi dhīrāḥ kecit pracaṇḍamṛgarājavadhe 'pi dakṣāḥ
children.translated_text: On earth there are some brave men who can split the frontal globes of intoxicated elephants; some are skilled even in killing a fierce lion.

children.text: kintu bravīmi balināṃ purataḥ prasahya kandarpadarpadalane viralā manuṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But I tell you: among the strong, men who can forcibly crush the pride of <s>Kandarpa</s> in his very presence are rare.

children.text: sanmārge tāvad āste prabhavati ca naras tāvad evendriyāṇāṃ lajjāṃ tāvad vidhatte vinayam api samālambate tāvad eva
children.translated_text: A man remains on the good path only so long, and has mastery over the senses only so long; he feels shame only so long, and maintains humility only so long,

children.text: bhrūcāpākṛṣṭamuktāḥ śravaṇapathagatā nīlapakṣmāṇa ete yāvallīlāvatīnāṃ hṛdi na dhṛtimuṣo dṛṣṭibāṇāḥ patanti ||
children.translated_text: as the arrow-like glances of graceful women, released from the bow of their eyebrows and feathered with dark lashes, do not fall along the path of his ears and steal firmness from his heart.

children.text: unmattapremasaṃrambhādārabhante yadaṅganāḥ
children.translated_text: When women begin something out of the tumult of frenzied love,

children.text: tatra pratyūham ādhātuṃ brahmāpi khalu kātaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: even <s>Brahmā</s>, surely, is afraid to place an obstacle there.

children.text: tāvan mahattvaṃ pāṇḍityaṃ kulīnatvaṃ vivekitā
children.translated_text: Greatness, learning, noble birth, and discrimination last only so long

children.text: yāvajjvalati nāṅgeṣu hataḥ pañceṣupāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the accursed fire of the five-arrowed god does not blaze in the limbs.

children.text: śāstrajño 'pi praguṇitanayo 'tyantabādhāpi bāḍhaṃ saṃsāre 'smin bhavati viralo bhājanaṃ sadgatīnām
children.translated_text: Even one who knows the śāstras, whose conduct is excellent, and who has endured extreme hardship in this world, is very rarely a vessel for good destinies,

children.text: yenaitasmin nirayanagaradvāram udghāṭayantī vāmākṣīṇāṃ bhavati kuṭilā bhrūlatā kuñcikeva ||
children.translated_text: when, for him, the crooked creeper of the eyebrows of left-glancing women becomes like a key opening the gate of the city of hell.

children.text: kṛśaḥ kāṇaḥ khañjaḥ śravaṇarahitaḥ pucchavikalo vraṇī pūyaklinnaḥ kṛmikulaśatair āvṛtatanuḥ
children.translated_text: Thin, one-eyed, lame, deaf, tail-mangled, ulcerous, wet with pus, his body covered by hundreds of worms,

children.text: kṣudhā kṣāmo jīrṇaḥ piṭharakakapālārpitagalaḥ śunīm anveti śvā hatam api ca hanty eva madanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: emaciated with hunger, old, with his neck thrust into the skull of a cooking pot, a dog still follows a bitch. Desire strikes even one already struck down.

children.text: strīmudrāṃ kusumāyudhasya jayinīṃ sarvārthasampatkarīṃ ye mūḍhāḥ pravihāya yānti kudhiyo mithyāphalānveṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Fools and wrong-minded men, seeking false rewards, abandon the conquering seal of the flower-weaponed god, which brings every kind of prosperity: woman.

children.text: te tenaiva nihatya nirdayataraṃ nagnīkṛtā muṇḍitāḥ kecit pañcaśikhīkṛtāś ca jaṭilāḥ kāpālikāś cāpare ||
children.translated_text: By that very god they are struck down most mercilessly: some are made naked and shaven, some given five tufts, some made matted-haired ascetics, and others skull-bearing ascetics.

children.text: viśvāmitraparāśaraprabhṛtayo vātāmbuparṇāśanāste 'pi strīmukhapaṅkajaṃ sulalitaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva mohaṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>, and others, who lived on wind, water, and leaves, still fell into delusion merely on seeing the lovely lotus-face of a woman.

children.text: śālyannaṃ saghṛtaṃ payodadhiyutaṃ ye bhuñjate mānavāsteṣām indriyanigraho yadi bhaved vindhyaḥ plavet sāgare ||
children.translated_text: If men who eat rice with ghee, milk, and curds could have restraint of the senses, then the <s>Vindhya</s> would float in the ocean.

children.text: parimalabhṛto vātāḥ śākhā navāṅkurakoṭayo madhuravidhurotkaṇṭhābhājaḥ priyā pikapakṣiṇām
children.translated_text: Fragrant winds, branches with tips of fresh shoots, and beloved cuckoo birds filled with sweet, plaintive longing,

children.text: viralavirasasvedodgārā vadhūvadanendavaḥ prasarati madhau dhātryāṃ jāto na kasya guṇodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the moon-like faces of brides giving off sparse, faint beads of sweat: when spring spreads over the earth, for whom does excellence not arise?

children.text: madhur ayaṃ madhurair api kokilākalaravair malayasya ca vāyubhiḥ
children.translated_text: This spring is sweet with the sweet warblings of cuckoos and with the winds of <s>Malaya</s>.

children.text: virahiṇaḥ prahiṇasti śarīriṇo vipadi hanta sudhāpi viṣāyate ||
children.translated_text: Alas, for embodied beings who are separated from their beloved, even nectar in adversity turns into poison.

children.text: āvāsaḥ kilakiñcitasya dayitāpārśve vilāsālasāḥ karṇe kokilakāminīkalaravaḥ smero latāmaṇḍapaḥ
children.translated_text: The dwelling-place of coy dalliance beside the beloved, languid with play; the tender cry of female cuckoos in the ear; the smiling bower of creepers;

children.text: goṣṭhī satkavibhiḥ samaṃ katipayair mugdhāḥ sudhāṃśoḥ karāḥ keṣāṃcit sukhayanti cātra hṛdayaṃ caitre vicitrāḥ kṣapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: conversation together with a few good poets; the charming rays of the moon: for some people here, the wondrous nights of <s>Caitra</s> delight the heart.

children.text: pāntha strīvirahānalāhutikalām ātanvatī mañjarīmākandeṣu pikāṅganābhir adhunā sotkaṇṭham ālokyate
children.translated_text: Traveler, now the mango-blossom cluster is looked upon with yearning by the female cuckoos, as it seems to extend the art of offering oblations into the fire of women's separation from their husbands.

children.text: apy ete navapāṭalāparimalaprāgbhārapāṭaccarā vāntiklāntivitānatānavakṛtaḥ śrīkhaṇḍaśailānilāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And these winds from the <s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s> mountain, scented with the powerful fragrance of fresh pāṭalā flowers, spread out a canopy that wearies the already weary.

children.text: prathitaḥ praṇayavatīnāṃ tāvat padam ātanotu hṛdi mānaḥ
children.translated_text: Let pride, famous among women in love, extend its footing in the heart only so long

children.text: bhavati na yāvaccandanatarusurabhir malayapavamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the <s>Malaya</s> breeze, fragrant with sandal trees, has not yet arisen.

children.text: sahakārakusumakesaranikara bharāmodamūrchitadigante
children.translated_text: When the quarters are faint with the heavy fragrance of masses of mango-blossom filaments,

children.text: madhuramadhuravidhuramadhupe madhau bhavet kasya notkaṇṭhā ||
children.translated_text: and when the bees are distressed by honey that is sweet upon sweet, in spring who would not feel longing?

children.text: acchācchacandanarasārdratarā mṛgākṣyo dhārāgṛhāṇi kusumāni ca kaumudī ca
children.translated_text: Clear, very cool sandal paste, moistened with juice; doe-eyed women; shower-houses; flowers; and moonlight,

children.text: mando marut sumanasaḥ śuci harmyapṛṣṭhaṃ grīṣme madaṃ ca madanaṃ ca vivardhayanti ||
children.translated_text: a gentle breeze, blossoms, a pure palace roof: in summer they increase both intoxication and love.

children.text: srajo hṛdyāmodā vyajanapavanaś candrakiraṇāḥ parāgaḥ kāsāro malayajarajaḥ śīdhu viśadam
children.translated_text: Garlands with heart-delighting fragrance, the breeze of fans, moonbeams, pollen, a pond, sandal dust from <s>Malaya</s>, and clear wine,

children.text: śuciḥ saudhotsaṅgaḥ pratanu vasanaṃ paṅkajadṛśo nidāghartāvetad vilasati labhante sukṛtinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a clean palace terrace, thin clothing, and lotus-eyed women: in the hot season the fortunate obtain these, and they shine.

children.text: sudhāśubhraṃ dhāma sphuradamalaraśmiḥ śaśadharaḥ priyāvaktrāmbhojaṃ malayajarajaś cātisurabhiḥ
children.translated_text: A dwelling white as nectar, the moon with flashing spotless rays, the lotus-face of the beloved, and sandal dust from <s>Malaya</s>, exceedingly fragrant;

children.text: srajo hṛdyāmodās tad idam akhilaṃ rāgiṇi jane karoty antaḥ kṣobhaṃ na tu viṣayasaṃsargavimukhe ||
children.translated_text: garlands with heart-delighting fragrance: all this produces inward agitation in a passionate person, but not in one turned away from contact with sense-objects.

children.text: taruṇīveṣoddīpitakāmā vikasajjātīpuṣpasugandhiḥ
children.translated_text: The rainy season, with desire kindled by the dress of young women, fragrant with blooming jāti flowers,

children.text: unnatapīnapayodharabhārā prāvṛṭ tanute kasya na harṣam ||
children.translated_text: and bearing the weight of high, full breasts, for whom does it not produce delight?

children.text: viyadupacitameghaṃ bhūmayaḥ kandalinyo navakuṭajakadambāmodino gandhavāhāḥ
children.translated_text: The sky swollen with clouds, the earth covered with sprouts, winds fragrant with fresh kuṭaja and kadamba blossoms,

children.text: śikhikulakalakekārāvaramyā vanāntāḥ sukhinam asukhinaṃ vā sarvam utkaṇṭhayanti ||
children.translated_text: and forest-edges lovely with the sweet cries of flocks of peacocks: they make everyone long, whether happy or unhappy.

children.text: upari ghanaṃ ghanapaṭalaṃ tiryag girayo 'pi nartitamayūrāḥ
children.translated_text: Above is a dense mass of clouds; sideways are mountains with dancing peacocks;

children.text: kṣitir api kandaladhavalā dṛṣṭiṃ pathikaḥ kva pātayati ||
children.translated_text: the earth too is white with sprouts: where can the traveler cast his gaze?

children.text: ito vidyudvallīvilasitam itaḥ ketakitaroḥ sphuran gandhaḥ prodyajjaladaninadasphūrjitam itaḥ
children.translated_text: Here is the play of lightning-creepers; there the bursting fragrance of the ketakī tree; here the thunderous roar of rising clouds;

children.text: itaḥ kekikrīḍākalakalaravaḥ pakṣmaladṛśāṃ kathaṃ yāsyanty ete virahadivasāḥ sambhṛtarasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: there the lovely clamor of playing peacocks: how will these days of separation, filled with passion, pass for women with thick-lashed eyes?

children.text: asūcisaṃcāre tamasi nabhasi prauḍhajaladadhvaniprājñaṃmanye patati pṛṣatānāṃ ca nicaye
children.translated_text: When the sky is dark, where even a needle cannot pass, and when a mass of raindrops is falling amid the loud, proud-seeming roar of mature clouds,

children.text: idaṃ saudāminyāḥ kanakakamanīyaṃ vilasitaṃ mudaṃ ca mlāniṃ ca prathayati pathi svairasudṛśām ||
children.translated_text: this golden, beautiful flash of lightning spreads both joy and dejection among independent fair-eyed women on the road.

children.text: āsāreṇa na harmyataḥ priyatamair yātuṃ bahiḥ śakyate śītotkampanimittam āyatadṛśā gāḍhaṃ samāliṅgyate
children.translated_text: Because of the downpour, one cannot go outside from the mansion with one's beloved; on the pretext of trembling from cold, a long-eyed woman is tightly embraced.

children.text: jātāḥ śīkaraśītalāś ca marutor atyantakhedacchido dhanyānāṃ bata durdinaṃ sudinatāṃ yāti priyāsaṅgame ||
children.translated_text: The winds have become cool with spray and cut off extreme fatigue: alas, for the fortunate, a bad-weather day becomes a good day in union with the beloved.

children.text: ardhaṃ suptvā niśāyāḥ sarabhasasuratāyāsasannaślathāṅgaprodbhūtāsahyatṛṣṇo madhumadanirato harmyapṛṣṭhe vivikte
children.translated_text: Having slept through half the night, exhausted and with limbs loosened by the exertion of eager love-play, tormented by unbearable thirst, delighting in wine and love on a secluded palace roof,

children.text: sambhogaklāntakāntāśithilabhujalatāvarjitaṃ karkarīto jyotsnābhinnācchadhāraṃ pibati na salilaṃ śāradaṃ mandapuṇyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the man of little merit does not drink autumn water from a jar, its clear stream split by moonlight, after his beloved, wearied by enjoyment, has withdrawn her slack creeper-like arms.

children.text: hemante dadhidugdhasarpiraśanā māñjiṣṭhavāsobhṛtaḥ kāśmīradravasāndradigdhavapuṣaś chinnā vicitrai rataiḥ
children.translated_text: In winter, eating curds, milk, and ghee, clothed in madder-red garments, their bodies thickly smeared with saffron liquid, exhausted by varied lovemaking,

children.text: vṛttorustanakāminījanakṛtāśleṣā gṛhābhyantare tāmbūlīdalapūgapūritamukhā dhanyāḥ sukhaṃ śerate ||
children.translated_text: embraced indoors by women with round thighs and breasts, their mouths filled with betel leaves and areca nuts, the fortunate sleep happily.

children.text: praduyatprauḍhapriyaṅgudyutibhṛti vikasatkundamādyaddvirephe kāle prāleyavātapracalavilasitodāramandāradhāmni
children.translated_text: At the season when mature priyaṅgu radiance shines forth, when blooming jasmine maddens the bees, and when the splendor of broad mandāra flowers is shaken by frosty winds,

children.text: yeṣāṃ no kaṇṭhalagnā kṣaṇam api tuhinakṣodadakṣā mṛgākṣī teṣām āyāmayāmā yamasadanasamā yāminī yāti yūnām ||
children.translated_text: for young men on whose neck a doe-eyed woman, skilled in crushing cold, is not clinging even for a moment, the long night passes like the house of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: cumbanto gaṇḍabhittīr alakavati mukhe sītkṛtānyādadhānā vakṣaḥsūtkañcukeṣu stanabharapulakodbhedam āpādayantaḥ
children.translated_text: Kissing cheek-walls, making sighing sounds in faces with loosened locks, causing the swelling of horripilation from the weight of breasts in tight bodices,

children.text: ūrūnākampayantaḥ pṛthujaghanataṭāt sraṃsayanto 'ṃśukāni vyaktaṃ kāntājanānāṃ viṭacaritabhṛtaḥ śaiśirā vānti vātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: shaking thighs, and making garments slip from broad hip-slopes: clearly the winter winds blow bearing the conduct of libertines toward beloved women.

children.text: keśānākulayan dṛśo mukulayan vāso balād ākṣipannātanvan pulakodgamaṃ prakaṭayann āvegakampaṃ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: Disordering the hair, closing the eyes, forcibly snatching garments, gradually producing an outburst of horripilation and revealing tremors of excitement,

children.text: vāraṃ vāram udārasītkṛtakṛto dantacchadān pīḍayan prāyaḥ śaiśira eṣa samprati marut kāntāsu kāntāyate ||
children.translated_text: again and again producing deep sighs and pressing the lips: this winter wind now seems, for the most part, to act as a lover toward beloved women.

children.text: yady asya nāsti ruciraṃ tasmiṃs tasya spṛhā manojñe 'pi
children.translated_text: If she has no taste for this charming thing, then, even though it is delightful, he has no desire for it.

children.text: ramaṇīye 'pi sudhāṃśau na manaḥkāmaḥ sarojinyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even in the lovely moon, the lotus-woman does not have the desire of her heart.

children.text: vairāgye saṃcaraty eko nītau bhramati cāparaḥ
children.translated_text: One person moves in detachment; another wanders in policy;

children.text: śṛṅgāre ramate kaścid bhuvi bhedāḥ parasparam ||
children.translated_text: someone delights in erotic love: on earth people's differences are mutual and many.

children.text: Chapter 3
cūḍottaṃsitacandracārukalikācañcacchikhābhāsvaro līlādagdhavilolakāmaśalabhaḥ śreyodaśāgre sphuran
children.translated_text: Radiant with a trembling flame, charming as a bud of the moon worn high on his crest, having playfully burned up the restless moth of <s>Kāma</s>, and flashing before the state of blessedness,

children.text: antaḥsphūrjadapāramohatimiraprāgbhāram uccāṭayan śvetaḥ sadmani yogināṃ vijayate jñānapradīpo haraḥ ||
children.translated_text: driving away the great mass of the darkness of boundless delusion that quivers within, white <s>Hara</s>, the lamp of knowledge, triumphs in the dwelling of yogins.

children.text: bhrāntaṃ deśam anekadurgaviṣamaṃ prāptaṃ na kiṃcit phalaṃ tyaktvā jātikulābhimānam ucitaṃ sevā kṛtā niṣphalā
children.translated_text: I have wandered through lands difficult and dangerous in many ways, and gained no fruit; abandoning the proper pride of birth and family, I have performed service, fruitlessly.

children.text: bhuktaṃ mānavivarjitaṃ paragṛheṣv āśaṅkayā kākavat tṛṣṇe jṛmbhasi pāpakarmapiśune nādyāpi saṃtuṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: In others' houses I have eaten food devoid of honor, fearfully, like a crow. O craving, informer of sinful deeds, you yawn wide; even now you are not satisfied.

children.text: utkhātaṃ nidhiśaṅkayā kṣititalaṃ dhmātā girer dhātavo nistīrṇaḥ saritāṃ patir nṛpatayo yatnena saṃtoṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: The surface of the earth has been dug up in the suspicion of treasure; the ores of mountains have been smelted; the lord of rivers, the ocean, has been crossed; kings have been satisfied with effort.

children.text: mantrārādhanatatpareṇa manasā nītāḥ śmaśāne niśāḥ prāptaḥ kāṇavarāṭako 'pi na mayā tṛṣṇe sakāmā bhava ||
children.translated_text: Nights have been spent in the cremation ground with a mind intent on propitiating mantras; yet not even a cowrie has been obtained by me. O craving, have your desire fulfilled!

children.text: khalālāpāḥ soḍhāḥ katham api tadārādhanaparairnigṛhyāntarbāṣpaṃ hasitam api śūnyena manasā
children.translated_text: The speeches of villains have somehow been endured by those devoted to winning their favor; inward tears have been restrained, and laughter too has been made with an empty mind.

children.text: kṛto vittastambhapratihatadhiyām añjalir api tvam āśe moghāśe kim aparam ato nartayasi mām ||
children.translated_text: Even folded hands have been made before those whose understanding was blocked by the pillar of wealth. O hope, vain hope, what more than this do you make me dance?

children.text: amīṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ tulitavisinīpatrapayasāṃ kṛte kiṃ nāsmābhir vigalitavivekair vyavasitam
children.translated_text: For the sake of these lives, which are comparable to water on a lotus-fiber leaf, what has not been undertaken by us, whose discrimination has slipped away?

children.text: yadāḍhyānām agre draviṇamadaniḥsaṃjñamanasāṃ kṛtaṃ māvavrīḍair nijaguṇakathāpātakam api ||
children.translated_text: Before the wealthy, whose minds are made senseless by intoxication with riches, we shamelessly committed even the sin of recounting our own virtues.

children.text: kṣāntaṃ na kṣamayā gṛhocitasukhaṃ tyaktaṃ na santoṣataḥ soḍho duḥsahaśītatāpapavanakleśo na taptaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Endurance was practiced, but not through forgiveness; the comfort proper to a home was abandoned, but not from contentment; the unbearable affliction of cold, heat, and wind was borne, but no austerity was performed.

children.text: dhyātaṃ vittam aharniśaṃ nityamitaprāṇair na śambhoḥ padaṃ tattatkarma kṛtaṃ yad eva munibhis tais taiḥ phalair vañcitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wealth was meditated on day and night with breaths constantly measured out, not the feet of <s>Śambhu</s>; just those actions were done which the sages do, but we have been cheated of those very fruits.

children.text: bhogā na bhuktā vayam eva bhuktāstapo na taptaṃ vayam eva taptāḥ
children.translated_text: Pleasures were not enjoyed; rather, we ourselves were consumed. Austerity was not practiced; rather, we ourselves were scorched.

children.text: kālo na yāto vayam eva yātāstṛṣṇā na jīrṇā vayam eva jīrṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Time has not passed; rather, we ourselves have passed away. Craving has not grown old; rather, we ourselves have grown old.

children.text: valibhir mukham ākrāntaṃ palitenāṅkitaṃ śiraḥ
children.translated_text: The face is invaded by wrinkles; the head is marked by gray hair.

children.text: gātrāṇi śithilāyante tṛṣṇaikā taruṇāyate ||
children.translated_text: The limbs grow slack, but craving alone grows young.

children.text: vivekavyākośe vidadhati same śāmyati tṛṣā pariṣvaṅge tuṅge prasaratitarāṃ sā pariṇatā
children.translated_text: When the sheath of discrimination opens, it becomes even and thirst is calmed; but when embraced at its height, that mature thirst spreads all the more.

children.text: jarājīrṇaiśvaryagrasanagahanākṣepakṛpaṇas tṛṣāpātraṃ yasyāṃ bhavati marutām apy adhipatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In it, even the lord of the winds becomes a vessel of thirst, wretchedly thrown into the thicket that devours an old-age-worn sovereignty.

children.text: nivṛttā bhogecchā puruṣabahumāno 'pi galitaḥ samānāḥ svaryātāḥ sapadi suhṛdo jīvitasamāḥ
children.translated_text: The desire for pleasures has ceased; men's high regard has also fallen away; companions, friends equal to life, have suddenly gone to heaven.

children.text: śanair yaṣṭyutthānaṃ ghanatimiraruddhe ca nayane aho mūḍhaḥ kāyas tad api maraṇāpāyacakitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Slowly one rises with a staff, and the eyes are obstructed by dense darkness. Ah, foolish body! Even then it trembles in fear of the danger of death.

children.text: āśā nāma nadī manorathajalā tṛṣṇātaraṅgākulā rāgagrāhavatī vitarkavihagā dhairyadrumadhvaṃsinī
children.translated_text: Hope is a river, with the water of imaginings, disturbed by the waves of craving, containing the crocodile of passion and the birds of conjecture, destroying the tree of firmness.

children.text: mohāvartasudustarātigahanā prottuṅgacintātaṭī tasyāḥ paragatā viśuddham alaso nandanti yogīśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Very hard to cross because of the whirlpools of delusion, exceedingly deep, with high banks of anxiety: having reached the far shore of that river, the pure and unwearied lords of yogins rejoice.

children.text: na saṃsārotpannaṃ caritam anupaśyāmi kuśalaṃ vipākaḥ puṇyānāṃ janayati bhayaṃ me vimṛśataḥ
children.translated_text: I do not see any wholesome conduct produced by <s>saṃsāra</s>; as I reflect, even the ripening of merits causes fear in me.

children.text: mahadbhiḥ puṇyaughaiś ciraparigṛhītāś ca viṣayā mahānto jāyante vyasanam iva dātuṃ viṣayiṇām ||
children.translated_text: For sense-objects, long secured by great floods of merit, become great as if in order to give calamity to sensualists.

children.text: avaśyaṃ yātāraś cirataram uṣitvāpi viṣayā viyoge ko bhedas tyajati na jano yat svayam amūn
children.translated_text: Sense-objects must inevitably go away, even after remaining for a very long time. What difference is there in separation, if a person does not abandon them himself?

children.text: vrajantaḥ svātantryād atulaparitāpāya manasaḥ svayaṃ tyaktā hy ete śamasukham anantaṃ vidadhati ||
children.translated_text: When they depart by their own independence, they bring incomparable torment to the mind; but when they are abandoned by oneself, they produce the endless happiness of tranquility.

children.text: brahmajñānavivekanirmaladhiyaḥ kurvanty aho duṣkaraṃ yanmuñcantyupabhogabhāñjyapi dhanānyekāntato niḥspṛhāḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, those whose intellects are purified by discernment and knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> do something difficult: utterly free from longing, they abandon wealth even when it is available for enjoyment.

children.text: samprāptān na purā na samprati na ca prāptau dṛḍhapratyayān vāñchāmātraparigrahān api paraṃ tyaktuṃ na śaktā vayam ||
children.translated_text: But we are unable to abandon even mere objects of desire, grasped only by wishing, neither obtained before, nor now, nor firmly believed to be obtainable.

children.text: dhanyānāṃ girikandareṣu vasatāṃ jyotiḥ paraṃ dhyāyatāmānandāśru jalaṃ pibanti śakunā niḥśaṅkam aṅkeśayāḥ
children.translated_text: For the blessed, dwelling in mountain caves and meditating on the supreme light, birds lying fearlessly in their laps drink the water of their tears of joy.

children.text: asmākaṃ tu manorathoparacitaprāsādavāpītaṭakrīḍākānanakelikautukajuṣām āyuḥ paraṃ kṣīyate ||
children.translated_text: But for us, devoted to the amusements of pleasure-groves, play, palace tanks, and mansions built up by imagination, life merely wastes away.

children.text: bhikṣāśataṃ tad api nīrasam ekavāraṃ śayyā ca bhūḥ parijano nijadehamātram
children.translated_text: A hundred alms, and that too tasteless, once a day; the earth as a bed; attendants consisting only of one's own body;

children.text: vastraṃ viśīrṇaśatakhaṇḍamayī ca kanthā hā hā tathāpi viṣayā na parityajanti ||
children.translated_text: a garment made of a patched cloak of a hundred torn pieces: alas, alas, even so sense-objects do not abandon us.

children.text: stanau māṃsagranthī kanakakalaśāv ity upamitī mukhaṃ śleṣmāgāraṃ tad api ca śaśāṅkena tulitam
children.translated_text: The breasts are lumps of flesh, yet compared to golden jars; the face is a storehouse of phlegm, and yet compared with the moon.

children.text: sravanmūtraklinnaṃ karivaraśiraspardhi jaghanaṃ muhur nindyaṃ rūpaṃ kavijanaviśeṣair gurukṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The hips, wet with flowing urine, rival the head of a noble elephant: this repeatedly blameworthy form has been made weighty by the special skill of poets.

children.text: eko rāgiṣu rājate priyatamādehārdhahārī haro nīrāgeṣu jano vimuktalalanāsaṅgo na yasmāt paraḥ
children.translated_text: Among the passionate, <s>Hara</s> alone shines, because he carries half the body of his beloved; among the dispassionate there is no one higher than he, because he is free from attachment to women.

children.text: durvārasmarabāṇapannagaviṣavyāviddhamugdho janaḥ śeṣaḥ kāmaviḍambitān na viṣayān bhoktuṃ na moktuṃ kṣamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rest of humankind, deluded after being pierced by the snake-poison of the irresistible arrows of <s>Smara</s>, mocked by desire, is able neither to enjoy sense-objects nor to give them up.

children.text: ajānan dāhātmyaṃ patatu śalabhas tīvradahane sa mīno 'py ajñānād baḍiśayutam aśnātu piśitam
children.translated_text: Let the moth fall into the fierce fire, not knowing its burning nature; let the fish too, through ignorance, eat the flesh furnished with a hook.

children.text: vijānanto 'py ete vayam iha viyajjālajaṭilān na muñcāmaḥ kānāmahaha gahano mohamahimā ||
children.translated_text: But we here, though we know, do not abandon these desires, tangled like a net in the sky. Ah, how deep is the greatness of delusion!

children.text: tṛṣā śuṣyaty āsye pibati salilaṃ śītamadhuraṃ kṣudhārtaḥ śālyannaṃ kavalayati māṃsādikalitam
children.translated_text: When thirst dries up his mouth, he drinks cool, sweet water; when tormented by hunger, he swallows rice-food mixed with meat and the like.

children.text: pradīpte kāmāgnau sudṛḍhataram āliṅgati vadhūṃ pratīkāraṃ vyādhaḥ sukham iti viparyasyati janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the fire of passion is blazing, he embraces his wife all the more tightly. Deluded people mistake a remedy for happiness.

children.text: tuṅgaṃ veśma sutāḥ satām abhimatāḥ saṅkhyātigāḥ sampadaḥ kalyāṇī dayitā vayaś ca navam ityajñānamūḍho janaḥ
children.translated_text: A lofty house, sons approved by the good, countless riches, an auspicious beloved, and fresh youth: the man stupefied by ignorance,

children.text: matvā viśvam anaśvaraṃ niviśate saṃsārakārāgṛhe saṃdṛśya kṣaṇabhaṅguraṃ tad akhilaṃ dhanyastu saṃnyasyati ||
children.translated_text: thinking the world imperishable, settles down in the prison-house of saṃsāra. But blessed is the man who, seeing that all of it is broken in a moment, renounces.

children.text: dīnā dīnamukhaiḥ sadaiva śiśukairākṛṣṭajīrṇāmbarā krośadbhiḥ kṣudhitair nirannavidhurā dṛśyā na ced gehinī
children.translated_text: If a housewife is not to be seen, poor, with a poor face, her worn-out garment constantly pulled by children crying from hunger and afflicted by lack of food,

children.text: yācñābhaṅgabhayena gadgadagalatruṭyadvilīnākṣaraṃ ko dehīti vadet svadagdhajaṭharasyārthe manasvī pumān ||
children.translated_text: what high-minded man, for the sake of his own accursed belly, would say, 'Give,' in words choked, broken, and dissolving from fear that his request will be rejected?

children.text: abhimatamahāmānagranthiprabhedapaṭīyasī gurutaraguṇagrāmābhojasphuṭojjvalacandrikā
children.translated_text: The belly-pot, very skilled at breaking the knots of cherished great pride, a bright moonlight for opening the lotuses that are masses of weighty virtues,

children.text: vipulavilallajjāvallīvitānakuṭhārikā jaṭharapiṭharī duṣpūreyaṃ karoti viḍambanam ||
children.translated_text: and an axe for the spreading creeper-canopy of vast, shining modesty, is hard to fill and makes a mockery of a person.

children.text: puṇye grāme vane vā mahati sitapaṭacchannapālī kapāliṃ hy ādāya nyāyagarbhadvijahutahutabhug dhūmadhūmropakaṇṭhe
children.translated_text: In a holy village or in a great forest, taking a skull-bowl covered by a white cloth, near a fire whose smoke has made the throat grey after twice-born men have offered oblations in due order,

children.text: dvāraṃ dvāraṃ praviṣṭo varam udaradarīpūraṇāya kṣudhārto mānī prāṇaiḥ sanātho na punar anudinaṃ tulyakulye sudīnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is better for a hungry but proud man, still supported by his life-breaths, to enter door after door merely to fill the cave of his belly, than to be utterly wretched day after day among people of equal family.

children.text: gaṅgātaraṅgakaṇaśīkaraśītalāni vidyādharādhyuṣitacāruśilātalāni
children.translated_text: Have the places of <s>Himavat</s>, cooled by sprays of drops from the waves of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and having charming stone slabs inhabited by vidyādharas,

children.text: sthānāni kiṃ himavataḥ pralayaṃ gatāni yat sāvamānaparapiṇḍaratā manuṣyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: gone to destruction, that human beings take pleasure in others' food while bearing humiliation?

children.text: kiṃ kandāḥ kandarebhyaḥ pralayam upagatā nirjharā vā giribhyaḥ pradhvastā vā tarubhyaḥ sarasagalabhṛto valkalinyaś ca śākhāḥ
children.translated_text: Have roots in the caves gone to destruction, or waterfalls from the mountains? Have the branches from trees, rich with juicy bark-garments, been destroyed,

children.text: vīkṣyante yan mukhāni prasabham apagatapraśrayāṇāṃ khalānāṃ duḥkhāptasvalpavittasmayapavanavaśānartitabhrūlatāni ||
children.translated_text: that the faces of wicked men, who have violently cast off courtesy and whose eyebrow-creepers are made to dance by the wind of pride from wealth painfully and slightly obtained, are gazed upon?

children.text: puṇyair mūlaphalais tathā praṇayinīṃ vṛttiṃ kuruṣvādhunā bhūśayyāṃ navapallavair akṛpaṇair uttiṣṭha yāvo vanam
children.translated_text: Now maintain a loving livelihood with pure roots and fruits. Rise from a ground-bed made generous with fresh shoots; let us go to the forest,

children.text: kṣudrāṇām avivekamūḍhamanasāṃ yatreśvarāṇāṃ sadā vittavyādhivikāravihvalagirāṃ nāmāpi na śrūyate ||
children.translated_text: where the very names of petty lords, whose minds are stupefied by lack of discernment and whose speech is bewildered by the disease and distortion of wealth, are never heard.

children.text: phalaṃ svecchālabhyaṃ prativanam akhedaṃ kṣitiruhāṃ payaḥ sthāne sthāne śiśiramadhuraṃ puṇyasaritām
children.translated_text: Fruit is obtainable at will in every forest, without toil, from the trees; cool, sweet water is found everywhere from sacred rivers.

children.text: mṛdusparśā śayyā sulalitalatāpallavamayī sahante santāpaṃ tad api dhanināṃ dvāri kṛpaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A bed, soft to the touch, is made of delicate creeper shoots. Yet pitiable men endure suffering at the doors of the rich.

children.text: ye vartante dhanapatipuraḥ prārthanāduḥkhabhājo ye cālpatvaṃ dadhati viṣayākṣepaparyāptabuddheḥ
children.translated_text: Those who stand before the lord of wealth and share the misery of petitioning, and those whose intellect has become petty through the force of sense-objects,

children.text: teṣām antaḥsphuritahasitaṃ vāsarāṇi smareyaṃ dhyānacchede śikharikuharagrāvaśayyāniṣaṇṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may I remember their laughter flashing within, while seated on a stone-bed in a mountain cave when meditation is interrupted.

children.text: ye santoṣanirantarapramuditas teṣāṃ na bhinnā mudo ye tv anye dhanalubdhasaṅkaladhiyas teṣāṃ na tṛṣṇāhatā
children.translated_text: For those who are continuously delighted by contentment, joys are not divided; but for others, whose thoughts are bound by greed for wealth, craving is not destroyed.

children.text: itthaṃ kasya kṛte kutaḥ sa vidhinā kīdṛkpadaṃ sampadāṃ svātmanyeva samāptahemamahimā merur na me rocate ||
children.translated_text: Thus, for whose sake, from where, and by fate in what position is wealth obtained? <s>Meru</s>, whose golden greatness is complete in itself, does not please me.

children.text: bhikṣāhāram adainyam apratisukhaṃ bhīticchidaṃ sarvato durmātsaryamadābhimānamathanaṃ duḥkhaughavidhvaṃsanam
children.translated_text: The great lords of yoga praise food obtained by begging: free from wretchedness, not dependent on another's pleasure, cutting off fear on every side, crushing bad envy, pride, and self-conceit, and destroying floods of suffering;

children.text: sarvatrānvaham aprayatnasulabhaṃ sādhupriyaṃ pāvanaṃ śambhoḥ satram avāyam akṣayanidhiṃ śaṃsanti yogīśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: available everywhere every day without effort, dear to the good, purifying, <s>Śambhu</s>'s feast, inexhaustible, and an imperishable treasure.

children.text: bhoge rogamayaṃ kule cyutibhayaṃ vitte nṛpālād bhayaṃ māne dainyabhayaṃ bale ripubhayaṃ rūpe jarāyā bhayam
children.translated_text: In enjoyment there is fear of disease; in family, fear of downfall; in wealth, fear from the king; in honor, fear of humiliation; in strength, fear of enemies; in beauty, fear of old age;

children.text: śāstre vādibhayaṃ guṇe khalabhayaṃ kāye kṛtāntād bhayaṃ sarvaṃ vastu bhayānvitaṃ bhuvi nṝṇāṃ vairāgyam evābhayam ||
children.translated_text: in learning, fear of disputants; in virtue, fear of the wicked; in the body, fear from Death. Everything belonging to human beings on earth is filled with fear; detachment alone is fearless.

children.text: ākrāntaṃ maraṇena janma jarasā cātyujjvalaṃ yauvanaṃ santoṣo dhanalipsayā śamamukhaṃ prauḍhāṅganāvibhramaiḥ
children.translated_text: Birth is overrun by death, and brilliant youth by old age; contentment by desire for wealth, the face of tranquility by the coquetries of mature women;

children.text: lokair matsaribhir guṇā vanabhuvo vyālair nṛpā durjanairasthairyeṇa vibhūtayo 'pyapahatā grastaṃ na kiṃ kena vā ||
children.translated_text: virtues by envious people, forest-lands by serpents, kings by bad men, and even powers by instability. What has not been seized by something?

children.text: ādhivyādhiśatair janasya vividhair ārogyam unmūlyate lakṣmīr yatra patanti tatra vivṛtadvārā iva vyāpadaḥ
children.translated_text: A person's health is uprooted by hundreds of various mental and bodily afflictions; wherever Fortune falls, misfortunes are there like open doors.

children.text: jātaṃ jātam avaśyam āśu vivaśaṃ mṛtyuḥ karoty ātmasāt tat kiṃ tena niraṅkuśena vidhinā yan nirmitaṃ susthiram ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is born, death quickly and helplessly makes its own. What, then, has been created firm by that unrestrained fate?

children.text: bhogās tuṅgataraṅgabhaṅgataralāḥ prāṇāḥ kṣaṇadhvaṃsinaḥ stokānyeva dināni yauvanasukhaṃ sphūrtiḥ priyāsu sthitā
children.translated_text: Enjoyments are unsteady, like the breaking of lofty waves; life-breaths perish in a moment; the days are very few; the happiness of youth is slight; excitement toward beloved women lasts only briefly.

children.text: tatsaṃsāram asāram eva nikhilaṃ buddhvā budhā bodhakā lokānugrahapeśalena manasā yatnaḥ samādhīyatām ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, having understood that the whole of saṃsāra is utterly without substance, wise teachers, with minds made gentle by compassion for the world, should apply effort to concentration.

children.text: bhogā meghavitānamadhyavilasatsaudāminīcañcalā āyur vāyuvighaṭṭitābjapaṭalīlīnāmbuvad bhaṅguram
children.translated_text: Enjoyments are flickering like lightning flashing in the midst of a bank of clouds; life is fragile like water hidden in a mass of lotus petals struck by wind.

children.text: līlā yauvanalālasās tanubhṛtām ity ākalayya drutaṃ yoge dhairyasamādhisiddhisulabhe buddhiṃ vidadhvaṃ budhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing quickly that the playful longings of youth in embodied beings are such, wise people, set your mind on yoga, where steadiness and the perfection of concentration are easily attained.

children.text: āyuḥ kallolalolaṃ katipayadivasasthāyinī yauvanaśrīrarthāḥ saṅkalpakalpā ghanasamayataḍidvibhramā bhogapūgāḥ
children.translated_text: Life is restless like a wave; the splendor of youth lasts only a few days; riches are like mere acts of imagination, and heaps of pleasures are like the play of lightning in the rainy season.

children.text: kaṇṭhāśleṣopagūḍhaṃ tad api ca na ciraṃ yat priyābhaḥ praṇītaṃ brahmaṇy āsaktacittā bhavata bhavamayāmbhodhipāraṃ tarītum ||
children.translated_text: Even what is bestowed by the radiance of a beloved, clasped in an embrace around the neck, does not last long. Fix your minds on <s>Brahman</s>, in order to cross beyond the ocean made of worldly existence.

children.text: kṛcchreṇāmedhyamadhye niyamitatanubhiḥ sthīyate garbhavāse kāntāviśleṣaduḥkhavyatikaraviṣamo yauvane copabhogaḥ
children.translated_text: In the womb one remains with the body constrained, painfully placed amid impurity; and in youth enjoyment is made harsh by the pain and turmoil of separation from the beloved.

children.text: vāmākṣīṇām avajñāvihasitavasatir vṛddhabhāvo 'nyasādhuḥ saṃsāre re manuṣyā vadata yadi sukhaṃ svalpam apyasti kiṃcit ||
children.translated_text: Old age dwells in the mocking contempt of women with lovely eyes; there is no other good thing. Tell me, O human beings, whether there is even the least happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: vyāghrīva tiṣṭhati jarā paritarjayantī rogāś ca śatrava iva praharanti deham
children.translated_text: Old age stands threatening like a tigress, and diseases strike the body like enemies.

children.text: āyuḥ parisravati bhinnaghaṭādivāmbho lokas tathāpyahitam ācaratīti citram ||
children.translated_text: Life trickles away like water from a broken pot; and yet people practice what is harmful. This is astonishing.

children.text: bhogā bhaṅguravṛttayo bahuvidhās tair eva cāyaṃ bhavastat kasyeha kṛte paribhramata re lokāḥ kṛtaṃ ceṣṭitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Enjoyments have fragile courses and are of many kinds, and this existence itself depends on them. For whose sake, here, do you wander, O people? Enough of exertions.

children.text: āśāpāśaśatāpaśāntiviśadaṃ cetaḥ samādhīyatāṃ kāmotpattivaśāt svadhāmani yadi śraddheyam asmadvacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let the mind be set in concentration, made clear by the pacification of hundreds of snares of hope, if our word, arising from the power of desire, is to be trusted in its own proper place.

children.text: sakhe dhanyāḥ kecit truṭitabhavabandhavyatikarā vanānte cittāntarviṣam aviṣayāśītviṣagatāḥ
children.translated_text: Friend, blessed are certain people whose entanglement in the bondage of existence has been broken, who at the forest edge have within the mind gone beyond the venomous serpent of sense-objects.

children.text: śaraccandrajyotsnādhavalagaganābhogasubhagāṃ nayante ye rātriṃ sukṛtacayacintaikaśaraṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They pass the night, charming with the expanse of sky made white by autumn moonlight, taking refuge solely in reflection on their accumulated merit.

children.text: brahmendrādimarudgaṇāṃs tṛṇakaṇān yatra sthito manyate yatsvādād virasā bhavanti vibhavās trailokyarājyādayaḥ
children.translated_text: When someone is established there, he regards the hosts of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s> as bits of grass; from tasting it, even powers such as sovereignty over the three worlds become flavorless.

children.text: bhogaḥ ko 'pi sa eva ekaḥ paramo nityodito jṛmbhate bhoḥ sādho kṣaṇabhaṅgure tad itare bhoge ratiṃ mā kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: That single, supreme enjoyment, of some inexpressible kind, rises eternally and expands. O good man, do not delight in those other enjoyments, which break in a moment.

children.text: sā ramyā nagarī mahān sa nṛpatiḥ sāmantacakraṃ ca tat pārśve tasya ca sā vidagdhapariṣat tāś candrabimbānanāḥ
children.translated_text: That city was lovely; that king was great; that circle of feudatories was there; beside him was that learned assembly, and those women with moon-disc faces.

children.text: udvṛttaḥ sa rājaputranivahas te vandinas tāḥ kathāḥ sarvaṃ yasya vaśād agāt smṛtipathaṃ kālāya tasmai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That proud troop of princes, those panegyrists, those stories: all have gone, by whose power, onto the path of memory. Homage to that <s>Kāla</s>, Time.

children.text: yatrānekaḥ kvacid api gṛhe tatra tiṣṭhaty athaiko yatrāpyekastadanu bahavastatra naiko 'pi cānte
children.translated_text: Where many once were, there at some time one remains in the house; and where there was one, afterwards there are many, and in the end not even one.

children.text: itthaṃ nayau rajanidivasau lolayan dvāv ivākṣau kālaḥ kalyo bhuvanaphalake krīḍati prāṇiśāraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus skillful <s>Kāla</s>, Time, plays on the board of the world with living beings as dice, shaking night and day as if they were two dice.

children.text: ādityasya gatāgatair aharahaḥ saṃkṣīyate jīvitaṃ vyāpārair bahukāryabhāragurubhiḥ kālo 'pi na jñāyate
children.translated_text: By the sun's comings and goings, life is diminished day by day; amid affairs heavy with the burden of many duties, time itself is not noticed.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā janmajarāvipattimaraṇaṃ trāsaś ca notpadyate pītvā mohamayīṃ pramādamadirām unmattabhūtaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: Seeing birth, old age, calamity, and death, no terror arises: the world has become mad by drinking the liquor of heedlessness made of delusion.

children.text: rātriḥ saiva punaḥ sa eva divaso matvā mudhā jantavo dhāvantyudyaminas tathaiva nibhṛtaprārabdhatattatkriyāḥ
children.translated_text: Thinking, vainly, "It is the same night again, the same day again," creatures run on, busy as before, with those same actions quietly begun.

children.text: vyāpāraiḥ punaruktabhūtaviṣayair itthaṃvidhenāmunā saṃsāreṇa kadarthitā vayam aho mohān na lajjāmahe ||
children.translated_text: By this kind of <s>saṃsāra</s>, with its affairs concerning objects that have occurred again and again, we have been abused. Alas, through delusion we are not ashamed.

children.text: na dhyānaṃ padam īśvarasya vidhivat saṃsāravicchittaye svargadvārakapāṭapāṭanapaṭur dharmo 'pi nopārjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Meditation on the feet of the Lord was not properly practiced for cutting off <s>saṃsāra</s>; nor was <s>dharma</s> accumulated, skilled at breaking open the doors of heaven.

children.text: nārīpīnapayodharoruyugalaṃ svapne 'pi nāliṅgitaṃ mātuḥ kevalam eva yauvanavanacchede kuṭhārā vayam ||
children.translated_text: The pair of firm breasts and thighs of a woman was not embraced even in a dream. We are merely axes cutting down the forest of our mother's youth.

children.text: nābhyastā prativādivṛndadamanī vidyā vinītocitā khaḍgāgraiḥ karikumbhapīṭhadalanair nākaṃ na nītaṃ yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Learning fit for the well-trained, able to subdue hosts of opponents, was not practiced; fame was not carried to heaven by sword-points that split the frontal globes of elephants.

children.text: kāntākomalapallavādhararasaḥ pīto na candrodaye tāruṇyaṃ gatam eva niṣphalam aho śūnyālaye dīpavat ||
children.translated_text: The juice of the tender sprout-like lip of the beloved was not drunk at moonrise. Youth has simply gone in vain, alas, like a lamp in an empty house.

children.text: vidyā nādhigatā kalaṅkarahitā vittaṃ ca nopārjitaṃ śuśrūṣāpi samāhitena manasā pitror na sampāditā
children.translated_text: Stainless learning was not acquired, nor was wealth obtained; service to the parents was not performed with a concentrated mind.

children.text: ālolāyatalocanāḥ priyatamāḥ svapne 'pi nāliṅgitāḥ kālo 'yaṃ parapiṇḍalolupatayā kākair iva preryate ||
children.translated_text: Beloved women with tremulous, wide eyes were not embraced even in a dream. This time is driven on, like crows, by greed for another's morsel.

children.text: vayaṃ yebhyo jātāś ciraparigatā eva khalu te samaṃ yaiḥ saṃvṛddhāḥ smṛtiviṣayatāṃ te 'pi gamitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those from whom we were born have surely long since passed away; those with whom we grew up have also been made objects of memory.

children.text: idānīm ete smaḥ pratidivasam āsannapatanā gatās tulyāvasthāṃ sikatilanadītīratarubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now here we are, approaching our fall day by day, come to the same condition as trees on the bank of a sandy river.

children.text: āyur varṣaśataṃ nṝṇāṃ parimitaṃ rātrau tadardhaṃ gataṃ tasyārdhasya parasya cārdham aparaṃ bālatvavṛddhatvayoḥ
children.translated_text: The lifespan of human beings is limited to a hundred years; half of that is gone in night, and of the other half, one half again is taken up by childhood and old age.

children.text: śeṣaṃ vyādhiviyogaduḥkhasahitaṃ sevādibhir nīyate jīve vāritaraṅgacañcalatare saukhyaṃ kutaḥ prāṇinām ||
children.translated_text: The remainder is spent with sickness, separation, sorrow, service, and the like. In life, more unsteady than a wave on water, whence can happiness come for living beings?

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ bālo bhūtvā kṣaṇam vai yuvā kāmarasikaḥ kṣaṇaṃ vittair hīnaḥ kṣaṇam api ca sampūrṇavibhavaḥ
children.translated_text: For a moment a man becomes a child; for a moment, indeed, a youth fond of desire; for a moment he is without wealth, and for a moment he is full of prosperity.

children.text: jarājīrṇair aṅgair naṭa iva valīmaṇḍitatanūr naraḥ saṃsārānte viśati yamadhānīyavanikām ||
children.translated_text: Then, with limbs worn out by old age and a body adorned with wrinkles like an actor, at the end of <s>saṃsāra</s> a man enters the curtain of <s>Yama</s>'s abode.

children.text: tvaṃ rājā vayam apy upāsitaguruprajñābhimānonnatāḥ khyātas tvaṃ vibhavair yaśāṃsi kavayo dikṣu pratanvanti naḥ
children.translated_text: You are a king; we too are raised high by the pride of wisdom gained from honored teachers. You are famous through wealth; poets spread our renown in the quarters.

children.text: itthaṃ mānadhanātidūram ubhayor apy āvayor antaraṃ yady asmāsu parāṅmukho 'si vayam apy ekāntato niḥspṛhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, since the wealth of self-respect makes the distance between us both very great, if you are turned away from us, we too are wholly free from longing.

children.text: arthānām īśiṣe tvaṃ vayam api ca girām īśmahe yāvadarthaṃ śūras tvaṃ vādidarpavyupaśamanavidhāvakṣayaṃ pāṭavaṃ naḥ
children.translated_text: You rule over wealth; we too rule over words according to their meaning. You are a hero; we have unfailing skill in the task of subduing the pride of disputants.

children.text: sevante tvāṃ dhanāḍhyā matimalahatayemām api śrotukāmāmayyapyāsthā na te cet tvayi mama nitarām eva rājann anāsthā ||
children.translated_text: The wealthy serve you; those whose minds are cleansed of stain desire to hear this speech of mine. If you have no regard for me, then I, O king, have even greater disregard for you.

children.text: vayam iha parituṣṭā valkalais tvaṃ dukūlaiḥ sama iha paritoṣo nirviśeṣo viśeṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Here we are fully content with bark-garments, while you are content with fine silk; contentment here is equal, and no distinction is a real distinction.

children.text: sa tu bhavatu daridro yasya tṛṣṇā viśālā manasi ca parituṣṭe ko 'rthavān ko daridraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let that man be poor whose craving is vast. When the mind is content, who is rich and who is poor?

children.text: phalam alam aśanāya svādu pānāya toyaṃ kṣitir api śayanārthaṃ vāsase valkalaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Fruit is enough for eating, sweet water for drinking, the earth too for lying down, and bark-cloth for clothing.

children.text: navaghanamadhupānabhrāntasarvendriyāṇāmavinayamanumantuṃ notsahe durjanānām ||
children.translated_text: I cannot bear to approve the insolence of wicked men whose every sense is bewildered by drinking the honey of fresh clouds.

children.text: aśnīmahi vayaṃ bhikṣām āśāvāso vasīmahi
children.translated_text: We eat alms; we wear the quarters as our garment.

children.text: śayīmahi mahīpṛṣṭhe kurvīmahi kim īśvaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: We sleep on the surface of the earth. What have we to do with lords?

children.text: na naṭā nā viṭā na gāyakā na ca sabhyetaravādacuñcavaḥ
children.translated_text: We are not actors, nor libertines, nor singers, nor clever speakers of courtly chatter.

children.text: nṛpam īkṣitum atra ke vayaṃ stanabhārānamitā na yoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who are we here to look upon a king? Nor are we women bent low by the weight of their breasts.

children.text: vipulahṛdayair īśair etaj jagaj janitaṃ purā vidhṛtam aparair dattaṃ cānyair vijitya tṛṇaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: This world was produced of old by broad-hearted lords, sustained by others, and given away by still others after conquering it like a blade of grass.

children.text: iha hi bhuvanāny anyair dhīrāś caturdaśa bhuñjate katipayapurasvāmye puṃsāṃ ka eṣa madajvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, other steadfast men enjoy the fourteen worlds here. What is this fever of pride in men over mastery of a few towns?

children.text: abhuktāyāṃ yasyāṃ kṣaṇam api na yātaṃ nṛpaśatairdhuvastasyā lābhe ka iva bahumānaḥ kṣitibhṛtām
children.translated_text: If not even a moment has passed on earth without hundreds of kings enjoying it, what great honor can there be for rulers in obtaining that permanent possession?

children.text: tadaṃśasyāpy aṃśe tadavayaleśe 'pi patayo viṣāde kartavye vidadhati jaḍāḥ pratyuta mudam ||
children.translated_text: Dull men become delighted instead, though they ought to feel despair, when they are lords of only a part of its part, even of a mere fragment of its portion.

children.text: mṛtpiṇḍo jalarekhayā balayatiḥ sarvo 'pyayaṃ nanvaṇuḥ svāṃśīkṛtya sa eva saṅgaraśatai rājñāṃ gaṇā bhuñjate
children.translated_text: This whole earth is surely a mere lump of clay, surrounded by a line of water, an atom indeed; yet groups of kings, after making it their own share, enjoy it through hundreds of battles.

children.text: ye dadyur dadato 'thavā kim aparaṃ kṣudrā daridraṃ bhṛśaṃ dhig dhik tān puruṣādhamān dhanakaṇān vāñchanti tebhyo 'pi ye ||
children.translated_text: Those who would give it, or those who receive it: what more can be said? They are small and extremely poor. Shame, shame on those lowest of men who desire particles of wealth even from them.

children.text: sa jātaḥ ko 'py āsīn madanaripuṇā mūrdhni dhavalaṃ kapālaṃ yasyoccair vinihitam alaṅkāravidhaye
children.translated_text: Some such man was born, on whose head the enemy of <s>Madana</s> placed a white skull high as an ornament.

children.text: nṛbhiḥ prāṇatrāṇapravaṇamatibhiḥ kaiścid adhunā namadbhiḥ kaḥ puṃsām ayam atuladarpajvarabharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, when some men bow with minds intent on saving their lives, what is this unequalled burden of feverish pride among men?

children.text: pareṣāṃ cetāṃsi pratidivasam ārādhya bahudhā prasādaṃ kiṃ netuṃ viśasi hṛdaya kleśakalitam
children.translated_text: O heart, why do you enter, full of distress, hoping to bring about favor by daily propitiating the minds of others in many ways?

children.text: prasanne tvayy antaḥsavayamuditacintāmaṇigaṇo viviktaḥ saṅkalpaḥ kim abhilaṣitaṃ puṣyati na te ||
children.translated_text: When you yourself are pleased, and within you there is a host of wish-fulfilling jewels born together with joy, what desired thing does a secluded resolve not nourish for you?

children.text: satyām eva trilokīsariti haraśiraścumbinīvacchaṭāyāṃ sadvṛttiṃ kalpayantyāṃ vaṭaviṭaprabhavair valkalaiḥ satphalaiś ca
children.translated_text: When the stream of the three worlds, the spray that kisses <s>Hara</s>'s head, truly exists, and when it provides honest livelihood with bark-garments and good fruits produced from banyan branches,

children.text: ko 'yaṃ vidvān vipattijvarajanitarujātīvaduḥkhāsikānāṃ vaktraṃ vīkṣeta duḥsthe yadi hi na bibhṛyāt sve kuṭumbe 'nukampām ||
children.translated_text: what wise man would look at the face of the distressed, painfully suffering from the intense pain born of the fever of calamity, if he did not feel compassion for his own family?

children.text: paribhramasi kiṃ mudhā kvacana citta viśrāmyatāṃ svayaṃ bhavati yad yathā bhavati tat tathā nānyathā
children.translated_text: Why do you wander in vain? Rest somewhere, O mind. Whatever happens of itself happens just so, not otherwise.

children.text: atītam ananusmarann api ca bhāvyasaṃkalpayannatarkitasamāgamānubhavāmi bhoga nāham ||
children.translated_text: Not remembering the past, and not planning the future, I experience enjoyments that arrive unexpectedly.

children.text: etasmād viramendriyārthagahanādāyāsakād āśrayaśreyomārgam aśeṣaduḥkhaśamanavyāpāradakṣaṃ kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Therefore cease at once from this wearisome thicket of sense-objects. Take refuge in the path of the highest good, skilled in the work of pacifying every suffering.

children.text: svātmībhāvam upaihi saṃtyaja nijāṃ kallolalolaṃ gatiṃ mā bhūyo bhaja bhaṅgurāṃ bhavaratiṃ cetaḥ prasīdādhunā ||
children.translated_text: Come to self-possession; abandon your own wave-tossed movement. Do not again resort to fragile delight in worldly existence. O mind, be calm now.

children.text: mohaṃ mārjaya tām upārjaya ratiṃ candrārdhacūḍāmaṇau cetaḥ svargataraṅgiṇītaṭabhuvām āsaṅgam aṅgīkuru
children.translated_text: Wipe away delusion; acquire devotion to the one whose crest-jewel is the crescent moon. O mind, accept attachment to the bank-lands of the heavenly river.

children.text: ko vā vīciṣu budbudeṣu ca taḍillekhāsu ca śrīṣu ca jvālāgreṣu ca pannageṣu saridvegeṣu ca capratyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who could place trust in waves, bubbles, flashes of lightning, fortunes, flame-tips, serpents, or river-currents?

children.text: cetaś cintaya mā ramāṃ sakṛd imām asthāyinīm āsthayā bhūpālabhrukuṭīkuṭīviharaṇavyāpārapaṇyāṅganām
children.translated_text: O mind, do not think with attachment on this <s>Ramā</s>, unstable even for a moment, a courtesan whose trade is wandering in the huts of kings' frowning brows.

children.text: kanthākañcukinaḥ praviśya bhavanadvārāṇi vārāṇasīrathyāpaṅktiṣu pāṇipātrapatitāṃ bhikṣām apekṣāmahe ||
children.translated_text: Wearing a patched cloak as our jacket, after entering the doorways of houses, we wait for alms fallen into our hand-bowls in the rows of streets of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

children.text: agre gītaṃ sarasakavayaḥ pārśvayor dākṣiṇātyāḥ paścāllīlāvalayaraṇitaṃ cāmaragrāhiṇīnām
children.translated_text: In front there is song and eloquent poets; at the sides are southerners; behind is the playful jingling of bracelets of women holding fly-whisks.

children.text: yadyastyevaṃ kuru bhavarasāsvādane lampaṭatvaṃ no ceccetaḥ praviśa sahasā nirvikalpe samādhau ||
children.translated_text: If it is really like this, then become greedy for tasting the flavor of worldly existence. If not, O mind, enter at once into undifferentiated <s>samādhi</s>.

children.text: prāptāḥ śriyaḥ sakalakāmadughās tataḥ kiṃ nyastaṃ padaṃ śirasi vidviṣatāṃ tataḥ kim
children.translated_text: Riches that milk forth every desire have been obtained; what then? A foot has been placed on the heads of enemies; what then?

children.text: sampāditāḥ praṇayino vibhavais tataḥ kiṃ kalpaṃ sthitās tanubhṛtāṃ tanavas tataḥ kim ||
children.translated_text: Lovers have been won by wealth; what then? Bodies of embodied beings have lasted for an aeon; what then?

children.text: bhaktir bhave maraṇajanmabhayaṃ hṛdisthaṃ sneho na bandhuṣu na manmathajā vikārāḥ
children.translated_text: There is devotion to <s>Bhava</s>; the fear of death and birth remains in the heart; there is no affection for kinsmen and no disturbances born from <s>Manmatha</s>.

children.text: saṃsargadoṣarahitā vijayā vanāntā vairāgyam asti kim itaḥ param arthanīyam ||
children.translated_text: Forest places, victorious and free from the fault of association, are there; detachment is there. What more than this is to be sought?

children.text: tasmād anantam ajaraṃ paramaṃ vikāsi tad brahma cintaya kim ebhir asadvikalpaiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore contemplate that infinite, undecaying, supreme, expansive <s>Brahman</s>. What use are these unreal constructions?

children.text: yasyānuṣaṅgiṇa ime bhuvanādhipatyabhogādayaḥ kṛpaṇalokamatā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: For the enjoyments beginning with lordship over the worlds, which cling to that, become matters esteemed by pitiable people.

children.text: pātālam āviśasi yāsi nabho vilaṅghya diṅmaṇḍalaṃ bhramasi mānasacāpalena
children.translated_text: You enter the netherworld, you go leaping beyond the sky, and by the fickleness of the mind you wander through the circle of the directions.

children.text: bhrāntyāpi jātu vimalaṃ katham ātmanīnaṃ na brahma saṃsarasi nirvṛtim eṣi yena ||
children.translated_text: Yet not even by mistake do you ever reach the pure <s>Brahman</s> within yourself, by which you would attain release from saṃsāra and come to peace.

children.text: kiṃ vedaiḥ smṛtibhiḥ purāṇapaṭhanaiḥ śāstrair mahāvistaraiḥ svargagrāmakuṭīnivāsaphaladaiḥ karmakriyāvibhramaiḥ
children.translated_text: What use are the <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>smṛtis</s>, readings of the <s>purāṇas</s>, the vast śāstras, and the bewildering rites and actions that yield only the fruit of dwelling in the village-hut of heaven?

children.text: muktvaikaṃ bhavaduḥkhabhāraracanāvidhvaṃsakālānalaṃ svātmānandapadapraveśakalanaṃ śeṣair vaṇigvṛttibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Apart from the one thing: entrance into the state of the bliss of one's own self, a fire at the end of time that destroys the construction of the burden of suffering in existence. What use are the rest, mere merchants' occupations?

children.text: nāyaṃ te samayo rahasyam adhunā nidrāti nātho yadi sthitvā drakṣyati kupyati prabhur iti dvāreṣu yeṣāṃ vacaḥ
children.translated_text: 'This is not the time for you; now the master is asleep in secret. If you stand here, the lord will see you and grow angry': such are the words of those at the doors.

children.text: cetas tān apahāya yāhi bhavanaṃ devasya viśveśitur nirdauvārikanirdayoktyaparuṣaṃ niḥsomaśarmapradam ||
children.translated_text: O mind, abandon them and go to the abode of the god, the lord of the universe, free from the harshness of pitiless doorkeepers' speech and giving freedom from humiliation.

children.text: yato meruḥ śrīmān nipatati yugāntāgnivalitaḥ samudrāḥ śuṣyanti pracuramakaragrāhanilayāḥ
children.translated_text: Since glorious <s>Meru</s>, wrapped in the fire at the end of an age, falls down, and the oceans, homes of abundant makaras and crocodiles, dry up,

children.text: dharā gacchaty antaṃ dharaṇidharapādair api dhṛtā śarīre kā vārtā karikalabhakarṇāgracapale ||
children.translated_text: and the earth, though held by the feet of the mountains, comes to an end, what is there to say of the body, trembling like the tip of a young elephant's ear?

children.text: gātraṃ saṃkucitaṃ gatir vigalitā bhraṣṭā ca dantāvalirdṛṣṭir nakṣyati vardhate badhiratā vaktraṃ ca lālāyate
children.translated_text: The limbs shrink, the gait falters, the row of teeth has fallen out, the sight fails, deafness increases, and the mouth drools.

children.text: vākyaṃ nādriyate ca bāndhavajano bhāryā na śuśrūṣate hā kaṣṭaṃ puruṣasya jīrṇavayasaḥ putro 'py amitrāyate ||
children.translated_text: His speech is no longer respected by his kinsmen, his wife does not attend to him; alas, the misery: for a man of worn-out age even his son turns into an enemy.

children.text: varṇaṃ sitaṃ śirasi vīkṣya śiroruhāṇāṃ sthānaṃ jarāparibhavasya tadā pumāṃsam
children.translated_text: When young women see the white color of the hairs on a man's head, the sign of humiliation by old age,

children.text: āropitāsthiśatakaṃ parihṛtya yānti caṇḍālakūpam iva dūrataraṃ taruṇyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they avoid that man, whose frame is a hundred bones set up together, and go far away as from a caṇḍāla's well.

children.text: yāvat svastham idaṃ śarīram arujaṃ yāvacca dūre jarā yāvaccendriyaśaktir apratihatā yāvat kṣayo nāyuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: As long as this body is healthy and free from disease, as long as old age is still far away, as long as the power of the senses is unobstructed, and as long as life has not ebbed away,

children.text: ātmaśreyasi tāvad eva viduṣā kāryaḥ prayatno mahān saṃdīpte bhavane tu kūpakhananaṃ pratyudyamaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: just so long should a wise person make great effort for the good of the self. When the house is already ablaze, what sort of undertaking is digging a well?

children.text: tapasyantaḥ santaḥ kim adhinivasāmaḥ suranadīṃ guṇodārān dārān uta paricarāmaḥ savinayam
children.translated_text: Shall we, practicing austerity, dwell by the river of the gods? Or shall we humbly serve noble wives rich in virtues?

children.text: pibāmaḥ śāstraughān uta vividhakāvyāmṛtarasānna vidmaḥ kiṃ kurmaḥ katipayanimeṣāyuṣi jane ||
children.translated_text: Shall we drink in floods of śāstra, or the nectar-flavors of various poems? We do not know what to do, when human life lasts only a few instants.

children.text: durārādhyāś cāmī turagacalacittāḥ kṣitibhujo vayaṃ tu sthūlecchāḥ sumahati phale baddhamanasaḥ
children.translated_text: These kings are hard to propitiate, their minds restless as horses; but we have large desires, our minds fixed on a very great reward.

children.text: jarā dehaṃ mṛtyur harati dayitaṃ jīvitam idaṃ sakhe nānyacchreyo jagati viduṣe 'nyatra tapasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Old age takes the body, death takes away the beloved life. Friend, there is no other good in the world for the wise apart from austerity.

children.text: māne mlāyini khaṇḍite ca vasuni vyarthe prayāte 'rthini kṣīṇe bandhujane gate parijane naṣṭe śanair yauvane
children.translated_text: When honor has withered, wealth has been broken, petitioners have gone away disappointed, kinsmen have diminished, attendants have departed, and youth has gradually vanished,

children.text: yuktaṃ kevalam etad eva sudhiyāṃ yajjahnukanyāpayaḥpūtāgrāvagirīndrakandarataṭīkuñje nivāsaḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: this alone is fitting for the wise: to dwell somewhere in a bower on the slope of a cave of the lord of mountains, on stones purified by the water of the daughter of <s>Jahnu</s>.

children.text: ramyāś candramarīcayas tṛṇavatī ramyā vanāntasthalī ramyaṃ sādhusamāgamāgatasukhaṃ kāvyeṣu ramyāḥ kathāḥ
children.translated_text: The moonbeams are delightful; delightful is a grassy woodland ground; delightful is the happiness that comes from meeting the good; delightful are stories in poetry.

children.text: kopopāhitabāṣpabindutaralaṃ ramyaṃ priyāyā mukhaṃ sarvaṃ ramyam anityatām upagate citte na kiṃcit punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Delightful is the face of the beloved, trembling with drops of tears brought on by anger. Everything is delightful when the mind has gone toward impermanence; otherwise nothing is.

children.text: ramyaṃ harmyatalaṃ na kiṃ vasataye śravyaṃ na geyādikaṃ kiṃ vā prāṇasamāsamāgamasukhaṃ naivādhikaprītaye
children.translated_text: Is not the palace-roof delightful to live on? Is not song and the like pleasant to hear? Or is the happiness of close union with one's beloved not for the greatest joy?

children.text: kintu bhrāntapataṅgakṣapavanavyāloladīpāṅkuracchāyā cañcalam ākalayya sakalaṃ santo vanāntaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And yet, reckoning all this to be unsteady like the shadow of a lamp-flame shaken by the night wind when moths are confused around it, the good have gone to the forest.

children.text: ā saṃsārāt tribhuvanam idaṃ cinvatāṃ tāt tādṛṅnaivāsmākaṃ nayanapadavīṃ śrotramārgaṃ gato vā
children.translated_text: Dear friend, from the beginning of saṃsāra, among those searching this three-worlded universe, no such one has come within the path of our eyes or the road of our ears:

children.text: yo 'yaṃ dhatte viṣayakariṇo gāḍhagūḍhābhimānakṣībasyāntaḥ karaṇakariṇaḥ saṃyamālānalīlām ||
children.translated_text: one who performs the sport of a binding-chain for the inner elephant, intoxicated by deep, hidden self-conceit, the elephant of sense-objects.

children.text: yad etat svacchandaṃ viharaṇam akārpaṇyam aśanaṃ sahāryaiḥ saṃvāsaḥ śrutam upaśamaikavrataphalam
children.translated_text: This free wandering at will, this unbeggarly food, this dwelling together with worthy people, this learning whose fruit is the single vow of tranquility,

children.text: mano mandaspandaṃ bahir api cirasyāpi vimṛśanna jāne kasyaiṣā pariṇatir udārasya tapasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this mind, gently stirring, and reflecting even outwardly after a long time: I do not know for which noble austerity this is the ripening.

children.text: jīrṇā eva manorathāś ca hṛdaye yātaṃ ca tad yauvanaṃ hantāṅgeṣu guṇāḥ vandhyaphalatāṃ yātā guṇajñair vinā
children.translated_text: The wishes in the heart are already worn out, and that youth has gone; alas, qualities in the limbs have become fruitless without those who know qualities.

children.text: kiṃ yuktaṃ sahasābhyupaiti balavān kālaḥ kṛtānto 'kṣamī hā jñātaṃ madanāntakāṅghriyugalaṃ muktvāsti nānyo gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is fitting? Mighty Time, Death himself, suddenly approaches and is unforgiving. Ah, I understand: apart from the pair of feet of the destroyer of <s>Madana</s>, there is no other refuge.

children.text: maheśvare vā jagatām adhīśvare janārdane vā jagadantarātmani
children.translated_text: Whether in <s>Maheśvara</s>, the lord of the worlds, or in <s>Janārdana</s>, the inner self of the world,

children.text: na vastubhedapratipattir asti me tathāpi bhaktis taruṇenduśekhare ||
children.translated_text: I have no apprehension of a difference in reality; nevertheless my devotion is to the one who bears the young moon as his crest.

children.text: sphuratsphārajyotsnādhavalitatale kvāpi puline sukhāsīnāḥ śāntadhvantisu rajanīṣu dyusaritaḥ
children.translated_text: When shall we, seated comfortably somewhere on a sandbank of the heavenly river, its surface whitened by abundant flashing moonlight, on nights whose darkness has become peaceful,

children.text: bhavābhogodvignāḥ śiva śiva śivety uccavacasaḥ kadā yāsyāmo 'targatabahulabāṣpākuladaśām ||
children.translated_text: distressed by the abundance of worldly existence and crying aloud, '<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>,' reach a state overwhelmed by abundant tears within?

children.text: mahādevo devaḥ sarid api ca saiṣā surasaridguhā evāgāraṃ vasanam api tā eva haritaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mahādeva</s> is the god; this river too is the river of the gods; a cave alone is the house; those very directions are the clothing.

children.text: suhṛdā kālo 'yaṃ vratam idam adainyavratam idaṃ kiyad vā vakṣyāmo vaṭaviṭapa evāstu dayitā ||
children.translated_text: This time is a friend; this vow is a vow without wretchedness. How much shall we say? Let the branch of a banyan tree itself be the beloved.

children.text: vitīrṇe sarvasve taruṇakaruṇāpūrṇahṛdayāḥ smarantaḥ saṃsāre viguṇapariṇāmāṃ vidhigatim
children.translated_text: When all one's property has been given away, with hearts filled with fresh compassion, remembering in saṃsāra the faulty outcome of fate's course...

children.text: vayaṃ puṇyāraṇye pariṇataśaraccandrakiraṇāstriyāmā neṣyāmo haracaraṇacintaikaśaraṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: We shall pass the nights in a holy forest, our only refuge the thought of <s>Hara</s>'s feet, while the rays of the autumn moon have fully ripened.

children.text: kadā vārāṇasyām amarataṭinīrodhasi vasan vasānaḥ kaupīnaṃ śirasi nidadhāno 'ñjalipuṭam
children.translated_text: When shall I live in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, on the bank of the divine river, wearing only a loincloth and placing my joined hands upon my head,

children.text: aye gaurīnātha tripurahara śambho trinayana prasīdetyākrośan nimiṣam iva neṣyāmi divasān ||
children.translated_text: and, crying out, 'O lord of <s>Gaurī</s>, destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, three-eyed one, be gracious,' pass my days as if they were but a moment?

children.text: udyāneṣu vicitrabhojanavidhis tīvrātitīvraṃ tapaḥ kaupīnāvaraṇaṃ suvastram amitaṃ bhikṣāṭanaṃ maṇḍanam
children.translated_text: In that city, varied arrangements of food are found in gardens, the fiercest austerity is there, the covering of a loincloth is abundant fine clothing, begging for alms is adornment;

children.text: āsannaṃ maraṇaṃ ca maṅgalasamaṃ yasyāṃ samutpadyate tāṃ kāśīṃ parihṛtya hanta vibudhair anyatra kiṃ sthīyate ||
children.translated_text: and near death itself arises there as something like an auspicious blessing. Alas, after abandoning that <s>Kāśī</s>, why should wise men stay anywhere else?

children.text: snātvā gāṅgaiḥ payobhiḥ śucikusumaphalair arcayitvā vibho tvā dhyeye dhyānaṃ niveśya kṣitidharakuharagrāvaparyaṅkamūle
children.translated_text: Having bathed with the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, having worshipped you, O lord, with pure flowers and fruits, and having fixed meditation upon the object of meditation at the foot of a stone couch in a mountain cave,

children.text: ātmārāmaḥ phalāśī guruvacanaratas tvatprasādāt smarāre duḥkhaṃ mokṣye kadāhaṃ samakaracaraṇe puṃsi sevāsamuttham ||
children.translated_text: when, O enemy of <s>Smara</s>, shall I, delighting in the self, eating fruits, and devoted to my teacher's word, by your grace be freed from the suffering produced by service to men whose hands and feet are alike?

children.text: ekākī niḥspṛhaḥ śāntaḥ pāṇipātro digambaraḥ
children.translated_text: Alone, without desire, tranquil, with my hand as my bowl and the quarters as my garment,

children.text: kadā śambho bhaviṣyāmi karmanirmūlanakṣamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when, O <s>Śambhu</s>, shall I become capable of uprooting <s>karma</s>?

children.text: pāṇiṃ pātrayatāṃ nisargaśucinā bhaikṣeṇa saṃtuṣyatāṃ yatra kvāpi niṣīdatāṃ bahutṛṇaṃ viśvaṃ muhuḥ paśyatām
children.translated_text: For those who make the hand their bowl, are content with naturally pure alms, sit wherever they may, and repeatedly see the world as much grass,

children.text: atyāge 'pi tanor akhaṇḍaparamānandāvabodhaspṛśā madhvāko 'pi śivaprasādasulabhaḥ sampatsyate yoginām ||
children.translated_text: even without giving up the body, touching the awareness of unbroken supreme bliss, some intoxication, easy through <s>Śiva</s>'s grace, will come to yogins.

children.text: kaupīnaṃ śatakhaṇḍajarjarataraṃ kanthā punas tādṛśī naiścintyaṃ nirapekṣabhaikṣyam aśanaṃ nidrā śmaśāne vane
children.translated_text: If there is a loincloth, extremely tattered with a hundred patches, and a ragged cloak like that again; if there is freedom from care, alms without dependence, food, sleep in a cremation ground or forest,

children.text: svātantryeṇa niraṅkuśaṃ viharaṇaṃ svāntaṃ praśāntaṃ sadā sthairyaṃ yogamahotsave 'pi ca yadi trailokyarājyena kim ||
children.translated_text: unrestrained wandering in independence, a mind always deeply peaceful, and steadiness even in the great festival of yoga, what use is kingship over the three worlds?

children.text: brahmāṇḍaṃ maṇḍalīmātraṃ kiṃ lobhāya manasvinaḥ
children.translated_text: For the high-minded, the whole egg of <s>Brahman</s> is merely a little circle: how could it tempt them to greed?

children.text: śapharīsphūrtenābdhiḥ kṣubdho na khalu jāyate ||
children.translated_text: The ocean is surely not stirred by the darting of a tiny fish.

children.text: mātar lakṣmi bhajasva kaṃcid aparaṃ matkāṅkṣiṇī mā sma bhūrbhogeṣu spṛhayālavas tava vaśe kā niḥspṛhāṇām asi
children.translated_text: Mother <s>Lakṣmī</s>, seek someone else; do not long for me. In pleasures your power is only a slight craving; what are you to those without desire?

children.text: sadyaḥ syūtapalāśapatrapuṭikāpātraiḥ pavitrīkṛtairbhikṣāvastubhir eva samprati vayaṃ vṛttiṃ samīhāmahe ||
children.translated_text: Now we seek our livelihood only from alms, made pure in little bowls of freshly sewn palāśa leaves.

children.text: mahāśayyā pṛthvī vipulam upadhānaṃ bhujalatāṃ vitānaṃ cākāśaṃ vyajanam anukūlo 'yam anilaḥ
children.translated_text: The earth is a great bed; the wide pillow is the creeper of the arm; the sky is a canopy; this favorable wind is a fan;

children.text: śaraccandro dīpo virativanitāsaṅgamuditaḥ sukhī śāntaḥ śete munir atanubhūtir nṛpa iva ||
children.translated_text: the autumn moon is a lamp. Joyful in union with the woman named Detachment, happy and peaceful, the sage of vast experience sleeps like a king.

children.text: bhikṣāśī janamadhyasaṅgarahitaḥ svāyattaceṣṭaḥ sadā hānādānaviraktamārganirataḥ kaścit tapasvī sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Some ascetic remains there, eating alms, free from attachment to crowds, always acting under his own control, devoted to a path detached from loss and gain,

children.text: rathyākīrṇaviśīrṇajīrṇavasanaḥ samprāptakanthāsano nirmāno nirahaṃkṛtiḥ śamasukhābhogaikabaddhaspṛhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with a seat made from a ragged cloak of worn-out clothes scattered in the street, without pride, without egoism, bound by a single longing for the enjoyment of the happiness of tranquility.
