children.text: caṇḍālaḥ kim ayaṃ dvijātir athavā śūdro 'tha kiṃ tāpasaḥ kiṃ vā tattvavivekapeśalamatir yogīśvaraḥ ko 'pi kim
children.translated_text: 'Is this man an outcaste, or a twice-born man, or perhaps a Śūdra? Is he an ascetic, or perhaps some lord of yogins with a mind refined by discernment of reality?'

children.text: ity utpannavikalpajalpamukharair ābhāṣyamāṇā janair na kruddhāḥ pathi naiva tuṣṭamanaso yānti svayaṃ yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Though addressed by people made talkative by such babbling doubts, yogins go their own way on the road, neither angry nor pleased in mind.

children.text: hiṃsāśūnyam ayatnalabhyam aśanaṃ dhātrā marutkalpitaṃ vyālānaṃ paśavas tṛṇāṅkurabhujas tuṣṭāḥ sthalīśāyinaḥ
children.translated_text: The creator has fashioned food that is free from violence and obtained without effort, like air: animals are satisfied, lying on the ground and eating shoots of grass for serpents.

children.text: saṃsārārṇavalaṅghanakṣamadhiyāṃ vṛttiḥ kṛtā sā nṛṇāṃ tām anveṣayatāṃ prayānti satataṃ sarvaṃ samāptiṃ guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For men whose intellects are capable of crossing the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, that way of life has been made; when they seek it, all virtues constantly come to completion.

children.text: gaṅgātīre himagiriśilābaddhapadmāsanasya brahmadhyānābhyasanavidhinā yoganidrāṃ gatasya
children.translated_text: On the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, seated in lotus posture fixed on a stone of the snowy mountain, gone into yogic sleep through the practice of meditation on <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: kiṃ tair bhāvyaṃ mama sudivasair yatra te nirviśaṅkāḥ kaṇḍūyante jaraṭhahariṇāḥ svāṅgam aṅge madīye ||
children.translated_text: what need will I have of those good days when old deer, fearless, scratch their own bodies against my limbs?

children.text: jīrṇāḥ kanthā tataḥ kiṃ sitam amalapaṭaṃ paṭṭasūtraṃ tataḥ kiṃ ekā bhāryā tataḥ kiṃ hayakarisugaṇair āvṛto vā tataḥ kim
children.translated_text: The patched cloaks are worn out; so what? Or there is a white spotless cloth of silk thread; so what? There is one wife; so what? Or one is surrounded by fine troops of horses and elephants; so what?

children.text: bhaktaṃ bhuktaṃ tataḥ kiṃ kadaśanam athavā vāsarānte tataḥ kiṃ vyaktajyotir na vāntarmathitabhavabhayaṃ vaibhavaṃ vā tataḥ kim ||
children.translated_text: Fine rice has been eaten; so what? Or bad food at day's end; so what? Whether the inner light, the fear of becoming churned within, is manifest or not, what of splendor either way?

children.text: pāṇiḥ pātraṃ pavitraṃ bhramaṇaparigataṃ bhaikṣyam akṣayyam annaṃ vistīrṇaṃ vastram āśādaśakam acapalaṃ talpam asvalpam urvīm
children.translated_text: For those whose pure bowl is the hand, whose inexhaustible food is alms obtained while wandering, whose broad garment is the ten directions, and whose steady bed is the ample earth,

children.text: yeṣāṃ niḥsaṅgatāṅgīkaraṇapariṇatasvāntasantoṣiṇas te dhanyāḥ saṃnyastadainyavyatikaranikarāḥ karma nirmūlayanti ||
children.translated_text: whose minds are satisfied, matured by accepting nonattachment, they are blessed: having renounced the whole mass of dealings born of wretchedness, they uproot <s>karma</s>.

children.text: trailokyādhipatitvam eva virasaṃ yasmin mahāśāsane tallabdhvāsanavastramānaghaṭane bhoge ratiṃ mā kṛthāḥ
children.translated_text: In the great doctrine in which lordship over the three worlds itself is tasteless, once you have obtained the garment of practice, do not take delight in the measured contrivance of pleasures.

children.text: bhogaḥ ko 'pi sa eka eva paramo nityoditā jṛmbhaṇe yatsvādād virasā bhavanti viṣayās trailokyarājyādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is one enjoyment, and that alone is supreme, in the expansion of what has eternally arisen; from tasting it, sense-objects, beginning with kingship over the three worlds, become flavorless.

children.text: mātar medini tāta māruti sakhe tejaḥ subandho jala bhrātar vyoma nibaddha eṣa bhavatām antyaḥ praṇāmāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: Mother Earth, father Wind, friend Fire, good kinsman Water, brother Sky: this is the final joined-hand salutation bound for you.

children.text: yuṣmatsaṅgavaśopajātasukṛtasphārasphurannirmalajñānāpāstasamastamohamahimā līne parabrahmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: By the power of association with you, the vastness of all delusion has been driven away by shining stainless knowledge born from abundant merit, and I am dissolved in <s>Parabrahman</s>.

children.text: śayyā śailaśilāgṛhaṃ giriguhā vastraṃ taruṇāṃ tvacaḥ sāraṅgāḥ suhṛdo nanu kṣitiruhāṃ vṛttiḥ phalaiḥ komalaiḥ
children.translated_text: Their bed is a slab of mountain rock, their house a mountain cave, their garment the bark of young trees; the deer are their friends, surely, and their livelihood among trees is with tender fruits.

children.text: yeṣāṃ nirjharam ambupānam ucitaṃ ratyai tu vidyāṅganā manye te parameśvarāḥ śirasi yari baddho na sevāñjaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those for whom drinking water from waterfalls is proper, and for delight a maiden named Knowledge, I think they are supreme lords, on whose head no joined hands of service are bound.

children.text: dhairyaṃ yasya pitā kṣamā ca jananī śāntiś ciraṃ gehinī satyaṃ mitram idaṃ dayā ca bhaginī bhrātā manaḥsaṃyamaḥ
children.translated_text: For the one whose father is firmness, whose mother is patience, whose wife has long been peace, whose friend is truth, whose sister is compassion, and whose brother is restraint of mind,

children.text: śayyā bhūmitalaṃ diśo 'pi vasanaṃ jñānāmṛtaṃ bhojanaṃ hyete yasya kuṭumbino vada sakhe kasmād bhayaṃ yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose bed is the surface of the earth, whose clothing is even the directions, whose food is the nectar of knowledge, tell me, friend: why should there be fear for a yogin who has these as his family?

children.text: aho vā hāre vā balavati ripau vā suhṛdi vā maṇau vā loṣṭe vā kusumaśayane vā dṛṣadi vā
children.translated_text: Whether on a necklace or on a snake, whether on a powerful enemy or on a friend, whether on a jewel or on a clod, whether on a bed of flowers or on a stone,

children.text: tṛṇe vā straiṇe vā mama samadṛśo yānti divasāḥ kvacit puṇyāraṇye śiva śiva śiveti pralapataḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether on grass or on a woman, my days pass with equal vision, somewhere in a holy forest, as I cry out, '<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>.'
